title.zh: 卷三十四 列傳第二十八: 文學
title.raw: 卷三十四 列傳第二十八: 文學 Volume 34: Men of Letters

sentences.zh: 易曰「觀乎人文以化成天下」，孔子曰「煥乎其有文章」也。

translations.literal: The Changes says, "Observe the patterns of culture to transform the empire"; Confucius said, "How splendid—there are patterns indeed."
translations.idiomatic: In the Book of Changes we read, "Look upon the patterns of culture and thereby transform the world"; Confucius said, "How radiant its patterns are."

sentences.zh: 自楚、漢以降，辭人世出，洛汭、江左，其流彌暢。

translations.literal: From Chu and Han downward, men of letters emerged generation after generation; at the bend of the Luo and south of the Yangzi, the current grew ever fuller.
translations.idiomatic: Since the age of Chu and Han, writers have appeared in every generation; at Luoyang and in the lands south of the Yangzi, the stream of letters has run ever wider.

sentences.zh: 莫不思侔造化，明並日月，大則憲章典謨，裨贊王道，小則文理清正，申紓性靈。

translations.literal: All thought to rival creation and match sun and moon in brightness; in great matters they took the canonical documents as their model and aided the kingly way, in small matters they kept literary pattern clear and gave voice to the inner spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Each sought to equal Heaven and Earth in craft and the sun and moon in brilliance; on the large scale they patterned themselves on the ancient canons to support the royal Way, on the small they refined clear prose to release what lay in the heart.

sentences.zh: 至於經禮樂，綜人倫，通古今，述美惡，莫尚乎此。

translations.literal: As for threading ritual and music, synthesizing human relations, penetrating past and present, and narrating good and evil, nothing surpasses this.
translations.idiomatic: For threading ritual and music, binding human relations, opening past and present, and telling good from evil, nothing stands higher.

sentences.zh: 後主嗣業，雅尚文詞，傍求學藝，煥乎俱集。

translations.literal: The Last Ruler succeeded to the enterprise, elegantly valued literary composition, sought the arts on every side, and gathered them in splendid array.
translations.idiomatic: When the Last Ruler came to the throne he prized fine writing, gathered learning from every quarter, and had brilliance heaped together.

sentences.zh: 每臣下表疏及獻上賦頌者，躬自省覽，其有辭工，則神筆賞激，加其爵位，是以搢紳之徒，咸知自勵矣。

translations.literal: Whenever ministers submitted memorials or presented rhapsodies and eulogies, he personally examined them; if the wording was skilled, his divine brush rewarded and stimulated them and added to their rank—thus the gentry all knew to urge themselves onward.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a subject sent up a memorial or offered a fu or song, he read it himself; if the diction was strong, his own hand praised and promoted the writer and raised his rank—so office-holders everywhere took the hint to strive.

sentences.zh: 若名位文學晃著者，別以功跡論。

translations.literal: Those whose fame, position, and literary learning shone prominently are discussed separately according to merit and deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Men whose names, offices, and letters stood out conspicuously are treated elsewhere, judged by achievement.

sentences.zh: 今綴杜之偉等學既兼文，備于此篇云爾。

translations.literal: What is compiled here now—Du Zhiwei and others whose learning combined with literature—is complete in this chapter, thus.
translations.idiomatic: What follows records Du Zhiwei and others who united scholarship with letters, gathered in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 徐伯陽 張正見 蔡凝 阮卓

translations.literal: Xu Boyang, Zhang Zhengjian, Cai Ning, Ruan Zhuo
translations.idiomatic: Xu Boyang; Zhang Zhengjian; Cai Ning; Ruan Zhuo

sentences.zh: 杜之偉

translations.literal: Du Zhiwei
translations.idiomatic: Du Zhiwei

sentences.zh: 杜之偉字子大，吳郡錢塘人也。

translations.literal: Du Zhiwei, styled Zida, was a native of Qiantang in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zhiwei, style name Zida, came from Qiantang in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 家世儒學，以三禮專門。

translations.literal: His family for generations practiced Confucian learning and specialized in the Three Rites.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his house had pursued Confucian study, with the Three Rites as their specialty.

sentences.zh: 父規，梁奉朝請，與光祿大夫濟陽江革、都官尚書會稽孔休源友善。

translations.literal: His father Gui was a Liang court attendant and was friendly with Jiang Ge of Jiyang, grand master for the bright and pure, and Kong Xiuyuan of Kuaiji, director of the ministry of punishment.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gui served Liang as a court attendant and was on close terms with Jiang Ge of Jiyang, grand master for the bright and pure, and Kong Xiuyuan of Kuaiji, director of the ministry of punishment.

sentences.zh: 之偉幼精敏，有逸才。

translations.literal: Zhiwei in youth was keen and clever, with outstanding talent.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Zhiwei was quick and sharp, with gifts beyond his years.

sentences.zh: 七歲，受尚書，稍習詩、禮，略通其學。

translations.literal: At age seven he received the Documents and gradually studied the Odes and Rites, gaining a rough mastery of those studies.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he took up the Documents, then little by little the Odes and Rites, until he had a working grasp of each.

sentences.zh: 十五，遍觀文史及儀禮故事，時輩稱其早成。

translations.literal: At fifteen he read widely in literature and history and in ritual precedents and old stories; men of his day called him precocious.
translations.idiomatic: By fifteen he had ranged through literature and history, ritual usage and antiquities; contemporaries hailed him as early-matured.

sentences.zh: 僕射徐勉嘗見其文，重其有筆力。

translations.literal: Vice Director Xu Mian once saw his writing and valued its force of brush.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Xu Mian once read his work and prized its vigor of style.

sentences.zh: 中大

translations.literal: Collation variant: Zhongda.
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: Zhongda.

translations.literal: Collation variant: (Datong).
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (Datong).

sentences.zh: 〔通〕元年，梁武帝幸同泰寺捨身，敕勉撰定儀註，〔一〕勉以臺閣先無此禮，召之偉草具其儀。

translations.literal: Collation variant: [Tong]; adopted reading: In year 1, Emperor Wu of Liang went in person to Tongtai Temple to offer his body, and ordered Mian to draft and fix the ritual regulations. Editorial footnote marker 1. Mian said the court had never had this rite before and summoned Zhiwei to draft the ritual in outline.
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: [Tong]; adopted reading: In the first year, Emperor Wu of Liang went to Tongtai Temple to "yield his person" in the Buddhist rite and ordered Mian to set down the ceremonial rules. [1] Mian replied that the palace had no precedent for it and called Zhiwei to sketch the forms.

sentences.zh: 乃啟補東宮學士，與學士劉陟等鈔撰群書，各為題目。

translations.literal: He was then appointed supplemental eastern-palace academician; with the academicians Liu Zhi and others he copied and compiled from the mass of books, each taking a topic.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made a supplemental academician in the eastern palace and, with Liu Zhi and the other academicians, excerpted the libraries, each assigned a theme.

sentences.zh: 所撰富教、政道二篇，皆之偉為序。

translations.literal: The two pieces he drafted, "Enriching Instruction" and "The Way of Government," both had prefaces by Zhiwei.
translations.idiomatic: Of the two treatises he wrote, "Enriching Instruction" and "The Way of Government," Zhiwei supplied the prefaces for both.

sentences.zh: 及湘陰侯蕭昂為江州刺史，以之偉掌記室。

translations.literal: When the Marquis of Xiangyin, Xiao Ang, became inspector of Jiang province, he made Zhiwei master of his secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Ang, Marquis of Xiangyin, took up the Jiangzhou inspectorate, he put Zhiwei in charge of his secretariat.

sentences.zh: 〔二〕昂卒，廬陵王續代之，又手教招引，之偉固辭不應命，乃送昂喪柩還京。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 2. When Ang died, the Prince of Luling, Xu, replaced him; he also sent a personal instruction to summon him, but Zhiwei firmly declined and would not accept the appointment, and instead escorted Ang's coffin back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: [2] When Ang died, Xiao Xu of Luling succeeded him and again wrote in his own hand to recruit Zhiwei; Zhiwei refused outright, saw Ang's bier home to the capital, and would not take the post.

sentences.zh: 仍侍臨

translations.literal: He still attended the Lin
translations.idiomatic: He still attended the Lin

translations.literal: Collation variant: (Cheng).
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (Cheng).

sentences.zh: 〔城〕公讀。

translations.literal: Collation variant: [city] duke in study.
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: [city]; adopted reading: He continued as companion to the Duke of Lincheng for his lessons.

sentences.zh: 〔三〕尋除揚州議曹從事、南康嗣王墨曹參軍，兼太學限內博士。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 3. Soon he was made staff officer for deliberation in Yang province, secretariat aide to the Prince of Nankang, and concurrent inner-limit erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: [3] Before long he was made deliberation staff officer in Yangzhou, secretariat aide to the Prince of Nankang, and at the same time an inner-limit erudite of the national university.

sentences.zh: 〔大同〕七年，〔四〕梁皇太子釋奠於國學，時樂府無孔子、顏子登哥詞，〔五〕尚書參議令之偉制其文，伶人傳習，以為故事。

translations.literal: Collation variant: [Datong]; adopted reading: In year 7, Editorial footnote marker 4. the Liang crown prince performed the libation sacrifice to Confucius at the national university; at the time the Music Office had no ascending-song lyrics for Confucius and Yan Hui. Editorial footnote marker 5. The secretariat deliberator ordered Zhiwei to compose the text; the musicians transmitted and practiced it, and it became precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: [Datong]; adopted reading: In the seventh year, [4] the Liang crown prince offered the Confucian libation at the national university. The Music Office then lacked ascending-song words for Confucius and Yan Hui; [5] the secretariat deliberator had Zhiwei write them. The performers learned and kept them, and they became custom.

sentences.zh: 轉補安前邵陵王田曹參軍，又轉刑獄參軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred and made field-office aide to the Prince of Shaoling, then moved to prison-office aide.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as field-office aide to the Prince of Shaoling, then as prison-office aide.

sentences.zh: 之偉年位甚卑，特以彊識俊才，頗有名當世，吏部尚書張纘深知之，以為廊廟器也。

translations.literal: Though Zhiwei's age and rank were very low, he was known throughout the age solely for strong memory and outstanding talent; Director of the Ministry of Personnel Zhang Zuan understood him deeply and regarded him as material for the state altar.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwei was still young and low in rank, yet his encyclopedic mind and sharp gifts had already made him a name; Personnel Director Zhang Zuan saw him clearly and treated him as a future pillar of the court.

sentences.zh: 侯景反，之偉逃竄山澤。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, Zhiwei fled and hid in mountains and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rose in rebellion, Zhiwei hid in the hills and marshes.

sentences.zh: 及高祖為丞相，素聞其名，召補記室參軍。

translations.literal: When the Founder became chief minister, he had long heard his name and summoned him as supplemental secretariat aide.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Founder was chief minister he had long known Zhiwei's reputation and called him in as a supplemental secretariat aide.

sentences.zh: 遷中書侍郎，領大著作。

translations.literal: He was moved to palace secretariat gentleman and concurrently headed the grand directorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace secretariat gentleman and at the same time directed the grand history office.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，除鴻臚卿，餘並如故。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, he was made grand master of splendid felicity; the rest of his posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took the throne he was made grand master of splendid felicity while keeping his other offices.

sentences.zh: 之偉啟求解著作，曰：「臣以紹泰元年，忝中書侍郎，掌國史，于今四載。

translations.literal: Zhiwei memorialized asking to be relieved of the directorate, saying: "Your servant, in Shaotai year 1, was honored as palace secretariat gentleman and has managed the national history for four years to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwei asked to resign the history directorship, writing: "In Shaotai year 1 (555) I was undeservedly made palace secretariat gentleman and have kept the national annals for four years now.

sentences.zh: 臣本庸賤，謬蒙盼識，思報恩獎，不敢廢官。

translations.literal: Your servant is by nature base and lowly and was wrongly favored with recognition; I think to repay grace and reward and dare not abandon office.
translations.idiomatic: I am by nature mean and unworthy, yet was noticed and favored; I wished to repay that kindness and did not dare leave my post.

sentences.zh: 皇曆惟新，驅馭軒、昊，記言記事，未易其人，著作之材，更宜選眾。

translations.literal: The imperial chronology is newly renewed; we are driven before the chariot of heaven—recording words and recording events is not easy to entrust to one man; talent for the directorate should rather be chosen from the many.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty is new, the court rides under broad heaven, and to set down speech and deed is work for no single hand; the post of compiler ought to go to worthier men.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞沈炯、尚書左丞徐陵、梁前兼大著作虞荔、梁前黃門侍郎孔奐，或清文贍筆，或彊識稽古，遷、董之任，允屬群才，臣無容遽變市朝，〔六〕再妨賢路。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Shen Jiong, left vice director Xu Ling, former Liang concurrent grand compiler Yu Li, and former Liang yellow-gate gentleman Kong Huan—some with clear writing and ample brush, some with strong memory and mastery of antiquity—the charge of Sima Qian and Dong Zhongshu truly belongs to this group of talents; your servant has no grounds to rush and change the court and market, Editorial footnote marker 6. and again obstruct the path of the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Shen Jiong, left vice director Xu Ling, Liang's former concurrent grand compiler Yu Li, and Liang's former yellow-gate gentleman Kong Huan—some write with clarity and fullness, some remember deeply and know the old—are fit for the work of Qian and Dong; I have no excuse to bolt from court again [6] and block better men.

sentences.zh: 堯朝皆讓，誠不可追，陳力就列，庶幾知免。

translations.literal: In Yao's court all yielded—truly not to be pursued; to offer one's strength and take one's place is what I hope may win exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Even in Yao's time men stepped aside—that cannot be matched now; let me serve where I belong, and perhaps I may be released.

sentences.zh: 」優敕不許。

translations.literal: " A gracious edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor's gracious edict refused him.

sentences.zh: 尋轉大匠卿，遷太中大夫，仍敕撰梁史。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to grand master of works, promoted to grand master for the palace, and still ordered to compile the History of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made grand master of works, then grand master for the palace, and still charged with compiling the Liang history.

sentences.zh: 永定三年卒，時年五十二。

translations.literal: In Yongding year 3 he died, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongding year 3 (559) he died at fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 高祖甚悼惜之，詔贈通直散騎常侍，賻錢五萬，布五十匹，棺一具，剋日舉哀。

translations.literal: The Founder deeply mourned and regretted him; an edict posthumously made him direct and upright attendant of the scattered cavalry, granted fifty thousand in funeral money, fifty bolts of cloth, one coffin, and fixed a day for mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder grieved him deeply and ordered him posthumously made direct and upright attendant of the scattered cavalry, with fifty thousand cash in funeral gift, fifty bolts of cloth, one coffin, and a set day for the mourning service.

sentences.zh: 之偉為文，不尚浮華，而溫雅博贍。

translations.literal: Zhiwei in writing did not pursue florid display but was warm, elegant, and broadly ample.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwei's prose shunned ornament; it was mild, refined, and rich.

sentences.zh: 所製多遺失，存者十七卷。

translations.literal: Much of what he composed was lost; seventeen scrolls survive.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his writings are gone; seventeen scrolls remain.

sentences.zh: 顏晃字元明，琅邪臨沂人也。

translations.literal: Yan Huang, styled Yuanming, was a native of Linyi in Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Huang, style name Yuanming, came from Linyi in Langye.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，好學，有辭采。

translations.literal: Orphaned young and poor, he loved learning and had literary grace.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father early and grew up poor, yet loved study and had a gift for words.

sentences.zh: 解褐梁邵陵王兼記室參軍。

translations.literal: On first leaving the sackcloth he was made concurrent secretariat aide to the Prince of Shaoling of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: On first taking office he became a concurrent secretariat aide on the Prince of Shaoling's staff under Liang.

sentences.zh: 時東宮學士庾信嘗使于府中，王使晃接對，信輕其尚少，曰「此府兼記室幾人」？

translations.literal: At the time the eastern-palace academician Yu Xin was once sent on mission to the prince's establishment; the prince had Huang receive and reply to him. Xin looked down on him for being young and said, "How many concurrent secretariat aides does this establishment have?"
translations.idiomatic: Once when eastern-palace academician Yu Xin was sent to the prince's house, the prince had Huang answer him. Xin, thinking him too young, asked, "How many concurrent secretariat aides has this establishment, anyway?"

sentences.zh: 晃答曰「猶當少於宮中學士」。

translations.literal: Huang replied, "Still fewer than the palace academics."
translations.idiomatic: Huang answered, "Still fewer than the academics inside the palace."

sentences.zh: 當時以為善對。

translations.literal: Men of the time regarded it as a fine retort.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries judged it a sharp reply.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，西奔荊州。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's turmoil he fled west to Jing province.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion he fled west to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 承聖初，除中書侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chengsheng he was made palace secretariat gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Chengsheng he was appointed palace secretariat gentleman.

sentences.zh: 時杜龕為吳興太守，專好勇力，其所部多輕險少年，元帝患之，乃使晃管其書翰。

translations.literal: At the time Du Kan was grand administrator of Wuxing and devoted himself solely to valor and force; his district had many reckless young men, and Emperor Yuan was troubled by this, so he had Huang oversee his correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: Du Kan was then grand administrator of Wuxing and cared only for bold fighting; his commandery teemed with hotheaded youths, which troubled Emperor Yuan, who put Huang in charge of Kan's documents.

sentences.zh: 仍敕龕曰：「卿年時尚少，習讀未晚，顏晃文學之士，使相毗佐，造次之閒，必宜諮稟。

translations.literal: He also instructed Kan: "You are still young; it is not too late to study and read. Yan Huang is a man of letters—have him assist you at your side; in every hurried matter you must consult and report."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also told Kan: "You are still young and can still learn. Yan Huang is a literary man—let him stand beside you; even in passing affairs you must ask his counsel."

sentences.zh: 」及龕誅，晃歸世祖，世祖委以書記，親遇甚篤。

translations.literal: When Kan was executed, Huang returned to Emperor Wen; Emperor Wen entrusted him with secretarial records and favored him with great intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: After Kan was killed, Huang entered Emperor Wen's service; the emperor gave him charge of documents and treated him with exceptional closeness.

sentences.zh: 除宣毅府中錄事，兼記室參軍。

translations.literal: He was made recorder of the Xuanyi establishment and concurrent secretariat aide.
translations.idiomatic: He was made recorder on the Xuanyi staff and concurrent secretariat aide.

sentences.zh: 永定二年，高祖幸大莊嚴寺，其夜甘露降，晃獻甘露頌，詞義該典，高祖甚奇之。

translations.literal: In Yongding year 2 the Founder visited the Great Zhuangyan Monastery; that night sweet dew descended, and Huang presented a eulogy on the sweet dew whose wording and sense were comprehensive and canonical; the Founder marveled at it greatly.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongding year 2 (558) the Founder went to the Great Zhuangyan Monastery; sweet dew fell that night, and Huang offered a "Sweet Dew" eulogy, learned and apt in phrasing—the Founder was astonished.

sentences.zh: 天嘉初，遷員外散騎常侍，兼中書舍人，掌詔誥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjia he was moved to supernumerary attendant of the scattered cavalry and concurrent palace secretariat attendant, in charge of edicts and commands.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianjia he rose to supernumerary attendant of the scattered cavalry and concurrent palace secretariat attendant, drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 三年卒，時年五十三。

translations.literal: In year 3 he died, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 3 (562) he died at fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 詔贈司農卿，謚曰貞子，并賜墓地。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made him minister of public works, gave the posthumous title Baron of Integrity, and granted a burial plot as well.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made minister of public works, titled Baron of Integrity, and given a grave plot besides.

sentences.zh: 晃家世單門，傍無戚援，而介然脩立，為當世所知。

translations.literal: Huang's family for generations was a single gate without collateral kin on either side, yet he stood apart and cultivated himself and was known to the age.
translations.idiomatic: His house was a lone branch without kin to lean on, yet he held himself upright and won notice in his time.

sentences.zh: 其表奏詔誥，下筆立成，便得事理，而雅有氣質。

translations.literal: His memorials and edict drafts were finished the moment the brush touched paper and at once hit the matter's core, yet were elegant in spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials and edicts from his hand came whole as soon as he wrote and always struck the point, yet kept a noble tone.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collection in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: A collection of twenty scrolls survives.

sentences.zh: 江德藻

translations.literal: Jiang Decao
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Decao

sentences.zh: 江德

translations.literal: Jiang De
translations.idiomatic: Jiang De

translations.literal: Collation variant: (Cao).
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (Cao).

sentences.zh: 〔藻〕字德藻，〔七〕濟陽考城人也。

translations.literal: Collation variant: [Decao]; styled Decao, Editorial footnote marker 7. a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: [Decao]; styled Decao, [7] from Kaocheng in Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 祖柔之，齊尚書倉部郎中。

translations.literal: His grandfather Rouzhi was a Qi director in the ministry of revenue's granaries section.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Rouzhi had been a Qi director in the granaries section of the revenue ministry.

sentences.zh: 父革，梁度支尚書、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His father Ge was Liang director of revenue and grand master for the bright and pure.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ge served Liang as director of revenue and grand master for the bright and pure.

sentences.zh: 德藻好學，善屬文。

translations.literal: Decao loved learning and was skilled at composition.
translations.idiomatic: Decao loved study and wrote well.

sentences.zh: 美風儀，身長七尺四寸。

translations.literal: His bearing was fine; he stood seven chi four cun in height.
translations.idiomatic: He was handsome in bearing, seven chi four cun tall.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，事親盡禮。

translations.literal: By nature he was utmost in filial piety and served his parents with full ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply filial and waited on his parents with complete propriety.

sentences.zh: 與異產昆弟居，恩惠甚篤。

translations.literal: He lived with half-brothers of a different mother and was very generous and affectionate among them.
translations.idiomatic: He dwelt with uterine brothers and was warm and generous toward them.

sentences.zh: 起家梁南中郎武陵王行參軍。

translations.literal: On first taking office he was a traveling aide on the staff of the Prince of Wuling, southern army lieutenant of the center.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a traveling aide on the Prince of Wuling's staff in the southern army of the center.

sentences.zh: 大司馬南平王蕭偉聞其才，召為東閤祭酒。

translations.literal: Grand marshal the Prince of Nanping, Xiao Wei, heard of his talent and summoned him as eastern-pavilion libationer.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Xiao Wei, Prince of Nanping, heard of his gifts and made him eastern-pavilion libationer.

sentences.zh: 遷安西湘東王府外兵參軍，尋除尚書比部郎，以父憂去職。

translations.literal: He was moved to outer-army aide on the Prince of Xiangdong's western staff, then made director in the ministry of punishment's comparison section, and left office on his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to outer-army aide on the western staff of the Prince of Xiangdong, then made a comparison-section director in the ministry of punishment, and resigned when his father died.

sentences.zh: 服闋之後，容貌毀瘠，如居喪時。

translations.literal: After the mourning period ended, his appearance was wasted and emaciated as if still in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning was over he was still gaunt and worn, as though the coffin had not long left the house.

sentences.zh: 除安西武陵王記室，不就。

translations.literal: He was made secretariat master to the Prince of Wuling of the western army but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed secretariat master to the Prince of Wuling on the western army staff but declined.

sentences.zh: 久之，授廬陵王記室參軍。

translations.literal: After a long while he was appointed secretariat aide to the Prince of Luling.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a long interval was he made secretariat aide to the Prince of Luling.

sentences.zh: 除廷尉正，尋出為南兗州治中。

translations.literal: He was made director of the Court of Judicial Review, then went out as senior aide of Nanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He became director of the Court of Judicial Review, then left the capital as senior aide of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 及高祖為司空、征北將軍，引德藻為府諮議。

translations.literal: When the Founder was minister of works and general who campaigns north, he brought Decao in as staff deliberator.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder was minister of works and northern campaign general, he drew Decao in as a staff deliberator.

sentences.zh: 轉中書侍郎，遷雲麾臨海王長史。

translations.literal: He was moved to palace secretariat gentleman and promoted to chief clerk to the Prince of Linhai of the cloud-banners guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace secretariat gentleman, then chief clerk to the Prince of Linhai in the cloud-banners guard.

sentences.zh: 陳臺建，拜尚書吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Chen court was established, he was appointed vice director in the ministry of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen was founded he was made vice director in the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，授祕書監，兼尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, he was made director of the secretariat and concurrently left vice director in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: At the Founder's accession he became director of the secretariat and concurrently left vice director in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: Soon, in his original office, he was additionally made palace secretariat attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was also made palace secretariat attendant while keeping his prior post.

sentences.zh: 天嘉四年，兼散騎常侍，與中書郎劉師知使齊，〔八〕著北征道理記三卷。

translations.literal: In Tianjia year 4 he was additionally made attendant of the scattered cavalry and, with palace secretariat gentleman Liu Shizhi, was sent as envoy to Qi; Editorial footnote marker 8. he composed Record of the Roads of the Northern Expedition in three scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjia year 4 (563) he was further made attendant of the scattered cavalry and, with Liu Shizhi of the palace secretariat, went on embassy to Qi; [8] he wrote Record of the Roads of the Northern Expedition in three scrolls.

sentences.zh: 還拜太子中庶子，領步兵校尉。

translations.literal: On return he was made junior mentor to the crown prince and concurrently colonel of footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Back home he was appointed junior mentor to the heir apparent and colonel of footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 頃之遷御史中丞，坐公事免。

translations.literal: Before long he was moved to censor-in-chief and was dismissed for a public-service offense.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made censor-in-chief, then removed for a fault in office.

sentences.zh: 尋拜振遠將軍、通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed general who shakes the distance and direct and upright attendant of the scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored as general who shakes the distance and direct and upright attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 自求宰縣，出補新喻令，政尚恩惠，頗有異績。

translations.literal: He asked on his own to govern a county and went out as magistrate of Xinyu; his government prized kindness and favor and achieved notable results unlike others.
translations.idiomatic: He sought a county post of his own accord and was sent out as magistrate of Xinyu, ruling with grace and leaving an unusual record.

sentences.zh: 六年，卒於官，時年五十七。

translations.literal: In year 6 he died in office, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he died in his post at fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 世祖甚悼惜之，詔贈散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen deeply mourned and regretted him; an edict posthumously made him attendant of the scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen grieved him deeply and posthumously made him attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 所著文筆十五卷。

translations.literal: Literary works he authored fill fifteen scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His writings fill fifteen scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子椿，亦善屬文，歷太子庶子、尚書左丞。

translations.literal: His son Chun was also skilled at composition and served as junior mentor to the heir apparent and left vice director in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chun also wrote well and rose to junior mentor to the heir apparent and left vice director in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 庾持字允德，〔九〕潁川鄢陵人也。

translations.literal: Yu Chi, styled Yunde, Editorial footnote marker 9. was a native of Yanling in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chi, style name Yunde, [9] came from Yanling in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 祖佩玉，宋長沙內史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Peiyu was Song interior governor of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Peiyu had been Song interior governor of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 父〔沙〕彌，〔一０〕梁長城令。

translations.literal: His father Collation variant: [Sha] Mi, Editorial footnote marker 10. was a Liang magistrate of Changcheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father, collation variant: [Sha] Mi, [10] had been magistrate of Changcheng under Liang.

sentences.zh: 持少孤，性至孝，居父憂過禮。

translations.literal: Chi was orphaned young; by nature he was utmost in filial piety and in mourning his father exceeded the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Chi lost his father early, was deeply filial by nature, and in mourning went beyond the prescribed rites.

sentences.zh: 篤志好學，尤善書記，以才藝聞。

translations.literal: With steadfast purpose he loved learning, especially excelled at documents and records, and was known for talent and arts.
translations.idiomatic: He was steadfast in study, especially skilled at documents and records, and won renown for talent and literary craft.

sentences.zh: 解褐梁南平王國左常侍、輕車河東王府行參軍，兼尚書郎，尋而為真。

translations.literal: On leaving the black lacquered cap he was made Left Regular Attendant of the Liang Prince of Nanping's kingdom, Acting Retainer of the Prince of Hedong's light-chariot establishment, and concurrently Master of Writing; soon he was made regular.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as left regular attendant in the Prince of Nanping's kingdom, acting retainer in the Prince of Hedong's light-chariot staff, and concurrent master of writing; soon he held the post in full.

sentences.zh: 出為安吉令，遷鎮東邵陵王府限外記室，兼建康令。

translations.literal: He went out as magistrate of Anji, was moved to out-of-quota recorder in the Prince of Shaoling's eastern establishment, and concurrently magistrate of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Anji, then became out-of-quota recorder to the Prince of Shaoling and concurrent magistrate of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 天監初，世祖與持有舊，〔一一〕及世祖為吳興太守，以持為郡丞，兼掌書翰，自是常依文帝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian, Emperor Wen and Chi had an old acquaintance, Editorial footnote marker 11. and when Emperor Wen became Administrator of Wu Xing, he made Chi assistant administrator of the commandery and put him in charge of documents; from then on Chi regularly relied on Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianjian, Emperor Wen and Chi were old acquaintances [11]. When Emperor Wen became administrator of Wu Xing, he made Chi assistant administrator and put him in charge of documents; from then on Chi always followed Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 文帝剋張彪，鎮會稽，又令持監臨海郡。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen overcame Zhang Biao and garrisoned Kuaiji, he again had Chi oversee Linhai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen defeated Zhang Biao and garrisoned Kuaiji, he again had Chi oversee Linhai commandery.

sentences.zh: 以貪縱失民和，為山盜所劫，幽執十旬，世祖遣劉澄討平之，持乃獲免。

translations.literal: Because of greedy license he lost the people's goodwill; mountain bandits seized him and held him in secret for a hundred days; Emperor Wen sent Liu Cheng to suppress them and pacify the region, and only then was Chi released.
translations.idiomatic: Through greedy excess he lost popular support; mountain bandits seized and held him in secret for a hundred days. Emperor Wen sent Liu Cheng to suppress them, and Chi was only then released.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，授安東臨川王府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the Mandate, Chi was appointed Adviser to the Pacifying-East Prince of Linchuan's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder received the Mandate, Chi was made adviser to the pacifying-east Prince of Linchuan's establishment.

sentences.zh: 天嘉初，遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was moved to Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tiancheng (560) he was promoted to left assistant director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 以預長城之功，封崇德縣子，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: For merit in the Changcheng campaign he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Chongde, fief three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For merit at Changcheng he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Chongde, with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 拜封之日，請令史為客，受其餉遺，世祖怒之，因坐免。

translations.literal: On the day of enfeoffment he asked a clerical officer to be his guest and accepted his gifts; Emperor Wen was angry and had him dismissed on that account.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he received his fief he entertained a clerical officer as guest and accepted his gifts; Emperor Wen was furious and dismissed him for it.

sentences.zh: 尋為宣惠始興王府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Adviser to the Propagating-Favor Prince of Shixing's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made adviser to the propagating-favor Prince of Shixing's establishment.

sentences.zh: 除臨安令，坐杖殺縣民免封。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Lin'an; for beating a county commoner to death he lost his enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Lin'an; for beating a county commoner to death he lost his fief.

sentences.zh: 〔一二〕

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 12.
translations.idiomatic: Note 12.

translations.literal: Collation variant: (qian).
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (qian).

sentences.zh: 〔還〕為給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Collation variant: (huan). He was made Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 〔一三〕除稜威將軍、鹽官令。

translations.literal: Editorial footnote marker 13. He was made General of Edge Glory and magistrate of Yanguan.
translations.idiomatic: [13] He was made General of Edge Glory and magistrate of Yanguan.

sentences.zh: 光大元年，遷祕書監，知國史事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangda he was moved to Director of the Secretariat and put in charge of national history.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangda year 1 (567) he was made director of the secretariat and put in charge of the national history.

sentences.zh: 又為少府卿，領羽林監。

translations.literal: He was again made Director of the Palace Storehouses and concurrently supervised the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made director of the palace storehouses and concurrently supervised the Feathered Forest guard.

sentences.zh: 遷太中大夫，領步兵校尉。

translations.literal: He was moved to Grand Master of Palace Affairs and concurrently Colonel of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand master of palace affairs and concurrently colonel of footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 太建元年卒，時年六十二。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taijian he died, aged sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 1 (569) he died, aged sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 詔贈光祿大夫。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 持善字書，每屬辭，好為奇字，文士亦以此譏之。

translations.literal: Chi was skilled at calligraphy; whenever he composed, he liked to use unusual characters, and men of letters also ridiculed him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Chi was skilled at calligraphy; whenever he wrote, he favored odd characters, and literary men mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in ten juan.

sentences.zh: 許亨字亨道，高陽新城人，晉徵士詢之六世孫也。

translations.literal: Xu Heng, styled Hendao, was a native of Xincheng in Gaoyang—sixth-generation descendant of the Jin Recluse Xu Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Heng, styled Hendao, came from Xincheng in Gaoyang, sixth-generation descendant of the Jin recluse Xu Xun.

sentences.zh: 曾祖珪，歷給事中，委桂陽太守，高尚其志，居永興之究山，即詢之所隱也。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Gui served as Attendant, was appointed Administrator of Guiyang, but honored his will and lived on Mount Jiu in Yongxing—the very place Xun had hidden.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Gui had been an attendant and was appointed administrator of Guiyang, but honored his own resolve and lived on Mount Jiu in Yongxing—the very retreat of Xu Xun.

sentences.zh: 祖勇慧，齊太子家令、冗從僕射。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yonghui was Liang Household Tutor to the Heir Apparent and Supernumerary Vice Director of the Masters of Writing for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yonghui had been Liang household tutor to the heir apparent and supernumerary vice director of the masters of writing for the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 父懋，梁始平天門二郡守、太子中庶子、散騎常侍，以學藝聞，撰毛詩風雅比興義類十五卷，述行記四卷。

translations.literal: His father Mao was Liang Administrator of the two commanderies of Shiping and Tianmen, Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent, and Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry; he was known for learning and arts and compiled Meaning and Categories of the Mao Odes' Winds, Elegies, and Hymns in fifteen juan and Records of Conduct in four juan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mao had been Liang administrator of Shiping and Tianmen, junior mentor to the heir apparent, and scattered-cavalry regular attendant; known for learning and the arts, he compiled Meaning and Categories of the Mao Odes' Winds, Elegies, and Hymns in fifteen juan and Records of Conduct in four juan.

sentences.zh: 亨少傳家業，孤介有節行。

translations.literal: Heng in youth transmitted the family profession; solitary and upright, he had integrity in conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Heng in youth carried on the family learning; solitary and upright, he was known for integrity.

sentences.zh: 博通群書，多識前代舊事，名輩皆推許之，甚為南陽劉之遴所重，每相稱述。

translations.literal: Broadly versed in all books, he knew much of former-age antiquities; elders of reputation all commended him, and the Nanyang Liu Zhibian especially valued him and often praised him to others.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered all books and knew former ages well; men of standing commended him, and Liu Zhibian of Nanyang especially prized him and often spoke of him.

sentences.zh: 解褐梁安東王行參軍，〔一四〕兼太學博士，尋除平西府記室參軍。

translations.literal: On leaving the black lacquered cap he was made Acting Retainer in the Prince of An Dong's establishment, Editorial footnote marker 14. concurrently Erudite of the Imperial University; soon he was made Recorder of the Pacifying-West establishment.
translations.idiomatic: He began as acting retainer in the Prince of An Dong's establishment [14], concurrently erudite of the imperial university; soon he became recorder of the pacifying-west establishment.

sentences.zh: 太清初，為征西中記室，兼太常丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiqing he was Central Recorder of the Pacifying-West Army and concurrently Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Taiqing (547) he was central recorder of the pacifying-west army and concurrently vice director of the imperial ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，避地郢州，會梁邵陵王自東道至，引為諮議參軍。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion he fled to Yingzhou; when the Liang Prince of Shaoling came by the eastern route, Heng was recruited as Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion he fled to Yingzhou; when the Liang Prince of Shaoling came by the eastern route, Heng was recruited as adviser.

sentences.zh: 王僧辯之襲郢州也，素聞其名，召為儀同從事中郎。

translations.literal: When Wang Sengbian attacked Yingzhou, having long heard his name, he summoned Heng as Acting Retainer of the Masters of Writing with the same powers as a full one.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sengbian attacked Yingzhou he had long heard of Heng and summoned him as acting retainer of the masters of writing with full powers.

sentences.zh: 遷太尉從事中郎，與吳興沈炯對掌書記，府朝政務，一以委焉。

translations.literal: He was moved to Retainer of the Masters of Writing to the Grand Marshal and, with Shen Jiong of Wuxing, jointly managed documents; court and government affairs were wholly entrusted to them.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to retainer of the masters of writing to the grand marshal and, with Shen Jiong of Wuxing, jointly managed documents; all court and government business was entrusted to them.

sentences.zh: 晉安王承制，授給事黃門侍郎，亨奉牋辭府，僧辯答曰：「省告，承有朝授，良為德舉。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin'an assumed the regency, Heng was appointed Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate; Heng submitted a memorial declining the staff post, and Sengbian replied: "Your report is received; I learn you have received a court appointment—a fine selection of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jin'an assumed the regency, Heng was appointed Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate; Heng submitted a memorial declining the staff post. Sengbian replied, "Your report is received; I learn you have a court appointment—a fine choice of virtue.

sentences.zh: 卿操尚惇深，文藝該洽，學優而官，自致青紫。

translations.literal: Your conduct is sincere and deep, your literary arts comprehensive; learning excellence fitting office—you would reach the purple ranks yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Your conduct is sincere and deep and your literary arts comprehensive; with learning fit for office you would reach the purple ranks on your own.

sentences.zh: 況久羈駿足，將成頓轡，匡輔虛闇，期寄實深。

translations.literal: Moreover long constrained, a swift horse about to be halted; to aid and correct in a vacant and dim hour, the hope placed in you is truly deep.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover you have long been constrained, a swift horse about to be reined in; to aid and correct in this vacant and dim hour, the hope placed in you is truly deep.

sentences.zh: 既欣遊處，用忘勞屈，而枳棘栖鵷，常以增歎。

translations.literal: Though glad you may roam freely and forget weariness, yet the thorn bush harboring a feng-bird—this always adds to my sighs.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am glad you may go freely and forget hardship, a feng-bird nesting in thorn bushes always adds to my sighs.

sentences.zh: 夕郎之選，雖為清顯，位以才升，差自無愧。

translations.literal: The choice of 'evening gentleman' is though clear and eminent; the post is risen to by talent—you need scarcely feel shame.
translations.idiomatic: The post of Gentleman of the Evening, though clear and eminent, is won by talent—you need feel little shame.

sentences.zh: 且卿始云知命，方騁康衢，未有執戟之疲，便深夜行之慨，循復來翰，殊用憮然。

translations.literal: Moreover you first said you knew your fate, were just racing on the broad way, had not yet the weariness of bearing halberds, yet already the grief of night travel—reading your letter again, I am quite disquieted.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover you first said you knew your fate and were racing along the broad road, had not yet the weariness of bearing halberds, yet already grieve at night travel—reading your letter again, I am deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 古人相思，千里命駕，素心不昧，寧限城闉，存顧之深，荒慚無已。」

translations.literal: Ancients in mutual longing would drive a thousand li; a pure heart is not obscured—how could city walls limit it? The depth of care you show leaves me endlessly ashamed."
translations.idiomatic: Ancients in longing would drive a thousand li; a pure heart is not dimmed—how could city walls limit it? The depth of your regard leaves me endlessly ashamed."

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，授中散大夫，領羽林監。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the Mandate, Heng was appointed Grand Master of the Palace and supervised the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder received the Mandate, Heng was made grand master of the palace and supervised the Feathered Forest guard.

sentences.zh: 遷太中大夫，領大著作，知梁史事。

translations.literal: He was moved to Grand Master of Palace Affairs and concurrently Grand Historiographer, in charge of Liang history.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand master of palace affairs and concurrently grand historiographer, in charge of Liang history.

sentences.zh: 初，僧辯之誅也，所司收僧辯及其子頠〔屍〕，〔一五〕於方山同坎埋瘞，至是無敢言者。

translations.literal: At first, when Sengbian was put to death, the responsible office seized Sengbian and his son Yan's Collation variant: (shi). corpse, Editorial footnote marker 15. and buried them together in one pit at Mount Fang; by this time none dared speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: When Sengbian was executed, the authorities seized him and his son Yan's corpse [15] and buried them together in one pit at Mount Fang; by then none dared speak of it.

sentences.zh: 亨以故吏，抗表請葬之，乃與故義徐陵、張種、孔奐等，相率以家財營葬

translations.literal: Heng as a former clerk submitted a memorial requesting burial; then with his old comrades Xu Ling, Zhang Zhong, Kong Huan, and others, they jointly used family wealth to prepare the funeral
translations.idiomatic: Heng, as a former clerk, submitted a memorial requesting burial; then he and his old comrades Xu Ling, Zhang Zhong, Kong Huan, and others jointly used family wealth to prepare the funeral

translations.literal: Collation variant: (ju).
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (ju).

sentences.zh: ，〔一六〕凡七柩皆改窆焉。

translations.literal: , Editorial footnote marker 16. all seven coffins were reburied.
translations.idiomatic: [16] all seven coffins were reburied.

sentences.zh: 初撰齊書并志五十卷，遇亂失亡。

translations.literal: He had first compiled the Qi History with treatises in fifty juan, but it was lost in the turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: He had first compiled the Qi History with treatises in fifty juan, but it was lost in the chaos.

sentences.zh: 後撰梁史，成者五十八卷。

translations.literal: Later he compiled the Liang History; what was completed came to fifty-eight juan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he compiled the Liang History; the completed portion ran to fifty-eight juan.

sentences.zh: 梁太清之後所製文筆六卷。

translations.literal: Literary writings composed after Liang's Taiqing period, six juan.
translations.idiomatic: Literary writings composed after Liang's Taiqing period, six juan.

sentences.zh: 子善心，早知名，官至尚書度支侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Shansin was known early and reached the post of Vice Director of Revenue in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shansin was known from youth and rose to vice director of revenue in the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 褚玠字溫理，河南陽翟人也。

translations.literal: Chu Yu, styled Wenli, was a native of Yangzhai in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yu, styled Wenli, came from Yangzhai in Henan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖炫，宋昇明初與謝朏、江效、劉俁入侍殿中，謂之四友。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Xuan, at the beginning of Song's Shengming era, entered attendance in the palace hall with Xie Tiao, Jiang Xiao, and Liu Yi and were called the Four Friends.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Xuan, at the start of Song's Shengming era, attended in the palace hall with Xie Tiao, Jiang Xiao, and Liu Yi and were called the Four Friends.

sentences.zh: 官至侍中、吏部尚書，諡貞子。

translations.literal: He reached Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Masters of Writing; posthumous title Viscount of Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to attendant-in-ordinary and director of the masters of writing, with posthumous title Viscount of Zhen.

sentences.zh: 祖澐，梁御史中丞。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yun was Liang Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yun was Liang imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 父蒙，太子舍人。

translations.literal: His father Meng was Attendant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Meng was attendant to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 玠九歲而孤，為叔父驃騎從事中郎隨所養。

translations.literal: Yu was orphaned at nine and was raised by his uncle, Acting Retainer of the Masters of Writing to the Flying Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was orphaned at nine and was raised by his uncle, acting retainer of the masters of writing to the flying-cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 早有令譽，先達多以才器許之。

translations.literal: From early on he had a fine reputation; elders for the most part commended his talent and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had a fine reputation; elders mostly commended his talent and capacity.

sentences.zh: 及長，美風儀，善占對，博學能屬文，詞義典實，不好豔靡。

translations.literal: When he grew up he had fine bearing, was skilled at repartee, broadly learned and able to compose, his phrasing classical and solid, and did not like florid excess.
translations.idiomatic: As he matured he had fine bearing, was skilled at repartee, broadly learned and able to compose; his style was classical and solid, without florid excess.

sentences.zh: 起家王府法曹，歷轉外兵記室。

translations.literal: He began his career as Legal Officer of a princely establishment and through transfers became Outer Army Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: He began as legal officer of a princely establishment and through transfers became outer-army recorder.

sentences.zh: 天嘉中，兼通直散騎常侍，聘齊，還為桂陽王友。

translations.literal: In the Tiancheng era he was concurrently Regular Attendant of Unimpeded Access, was sent as envoy to Qi, and on return became Friend to the Prince of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tiancheng era he was concurrently regular attendant of unimpeded access, was envoy to Qi, and on return became friend to the Prince of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 遷太子庶子、中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was moved to Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent and Master of Writing Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to junior mentor to the heir apparent and master of writing attendant.

sentences.zh: 太建中，山陰縣多豪猾，前後令皆以贓汙免，高宗患之，謂中書舍人蔡景歷曰：「稽陰大邑，久無良宰，卿文士之內，試思其人。

translations.literal: In the Taijian era Shanyin county had many powerful ruffians; successive magistrates were all dismissed for bribery and corruption; Emperor Gaozong was troubled by this and said to Master of Writing Attendant Cai Jingli: "Ji Yin is a great county and long without a good magistrate; among men of letters, try to think of someone.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taijian era Shanyin county had many powerful ruffians and successive magistrates were dismissed for bribery; Emperor Gaozong was troubled and told master of writing attendant Cai Jingli, "Shanyin is a great county long without a good magistrate; among literary men, think of someone."

sentences.zh: 」景歷進曰：「褚玠廉儉有幹用，未審堪其選不？

translations.literal: " Jingli advanced and said: "Chu Yu is frugal and has practical ability—would he be unknown to be fit for the selection?
translations.idiomatic: " Jingli replied, "Chu Yu is frugal and capable—would he be unknown whether he fits the post?"

sentences.zh: 」高宗曰：「甚善，卿言與朕意同。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong said: "Very good—your words match my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong said, "Excellent—your words match my intent."

sentences.zh: 」乃除戎昭將軍、山陰令。

translations.literal: " He was then made General of Military Glory and magistrate of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was then made General of Military Glory and magistrate of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 縣民張次的、王休達等與諸猾吏賄賂通姦，全丁大戶，類多隱沒。

translations.literal: County commoners Zhang Cide and Wang Xiuda and others bribed and colluded with crafty clerks; whole-household great families for the most part concealed their registers.
translations.idiomatic: County commoners Zhang Cide and Wang Xiuda and others bribed crafty clerks; great households for the most part concealed their registers.

sentences.zh: 玠乃鎖次的等，具狀啟臺，高宗手敕慰勞，并遣使助玠搜括，所出軍民八百餘戶。

translations.literal: Yu then locked up Cide and the rest, submitted a full report to the capital, and Emperor Gaozong personally wrote in consolation and reward and also sent envoys to help Yu search and register; more than eight hundred military and civilian households were brought out.
translations.idiomatic: Yu then imprisoned Cide and the rest and submitted a full report to the capital; Emperor Gaozong personally wrote to console and reward him and sent envoys to help Yu search the registers, exposing more than eight hundred military and civilian households.

sentences.zh: 時舍人曹義達為高宗所寵，縣民陳信家富於財，諂事義達，信父顯文恃勢橫暴。

translations.literal: At the time Attendant Cao Yida was favored by Emperor Gaozong; county commoner Chen Xin was rich in wealth and fawned on Yida; Xin's father Xianwen relied on influence and acted violently.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Cao Yida was then favored by Emperor Gaozong; county commoner Chen Xin was wealthy and fawned on Yida; Xin's father Xianwen relied on power and acted violently.

sentences.zh: 玠乃遣使執顯文，鞭之一百，於是吏民股慄，莫敢犯者。

translations.literal: Yu then sent officers to seize Xianwen and gave him a hundred strokes of the whip; from then on clerks and people trembled and none dared offend.
translations.idiomatic: Yu then sent officers to seize Xianwen and gave him a hundred strokes of the whip; thereafter clerks and people trembled and none dared offend.

sentences.zh: 信後因義達譖玠，竟坐免官。

translations.literal: Later Xin, through Yida, slandered Yu, and in the end Yu was dismissed from office on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xin slandered Yu through Yida, and Yu was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 玠在任歲餘，守祿俸而已，去官之日，不堪自致，因留縣境，種蔬菜以自給。

translations.literal: Yu in office for more than a year kept only his salary; on the day he left office he could not support himself on the journey and therefore remained within the county border, planting vegetables to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yu held office for more than a year and kept only his salary; when he left he could not afford the journey and stayed within the county, planting vegetables to live.

sentences.zh: 或嗤玠以非百里之才，玠答曰：「吾委輸課最，不後列城，除殘去暴，姦吏局蹐。

translations.literal: Some mocked Yu as lacking the talent of a hundred-li magistrate; Yu replied: "My delivery of taxes and ranking among commanderies is not behind other cities; in removing the violent and ridding the cruel, crafty clerks cowered.
translations.idiomatic: Some mocked Yu as unfit for a county magistrate; Yu replied, "My tax deliveries and rankings are not behind other cities; in removing violence and ridding cruelty, crafty clerks cowered.

sentences.zh: 若謂其不能自潤脂膏，則如來命。

translations.literal: If you mean I could not enrich myself with grease and ointment, that is as fate ordained.
translations.idiomatic: If you mean I could not enrich myself with bribes, that is as fate ordained.

sentences.zh: 以為不達從政，吾未服也。

translations.literal: To say I did not understand governing—I am not convinced.
translations.idiomatic: To say I did not understand governing—I am not convinced.

sentences.zh: 」時人以為信然。

translations.literal: Men of the time held this credible.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the time found this credible.

sentences.zh: 皇太子知玠無還裝，手書賜粟米二百斛，於是還都。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent knew Yu had no travel funds; he personally wrote and granted two hundred piculs of grain and millet, and Yu then returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent knew Yu had no travel funds and personally wrote to grant him two hundred piculs of grain and millet; Yu then returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 太子愛玠文辭，令入直殿省。

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent loved Yu's literary compositions and had him enter attendance in the Hall Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent admired Yu's writing and had him attend in the hall directorate.

sentences.zh: 十年，除電威將軍、仁威淮南王長史，頃之，以本官掌東宮管記。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was made General of Lightning Might and Long Recorder to the Prince of Huainan of Renwei; soon he held his former post and concurrently managed Eastern Palace records.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 he was made General of Lightning Might and long recorder to the Prince of Huainan of Renwei; soon he held the same rank and concurrently managed eastern-palace records.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遷御史中丞，卒于官，時年五十二。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was moved to Imperial Censor and died in office, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he was made imperial censor and died in office, aged fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 玠剛毅有膽決，兼善騎射。

translations.literal: Yu was resolute and had bold decision; he was also skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was resolute and bold in decision; he was also skilled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 嘗從司空侯安都於徐州出獵，遇有猛獸，〔一七〕玠引弓射之，再發皆中口入腹，俄而獸斃。

translations.literal: Once he followed Minister of Works Hou Andu on a hunt at Xuzhou; they encountered a fierce beast, Editorial footnote marker 17. Yu drew his bow and shot; twice he hit the mouth entering the belly, and soon the beast fell dead.
translations.idiomatic: Once he followed Minister of Works Hou Andu hunting at Xuzhou; they met a fierce beast [17]. Yu drew his bow and shot twice, both entering the mouth into the belly, and the beast soon fell dead.

sentences.zh: 及為御史中丞，甚有直繩之稱。

translations.literal: When he was Imperial Censor he had a great reputation for the straight cord.
translations.idiomatic: As imperial censor he won a great reputation for upholding the law.

sentences.zh: 自梁末喪亂，朝章廢弛，司憲因循，守而勿革，玠方欲改張，大為條例，綱維略舉，而編次未訖，故不列于後焉。

translations.literal: From the end of Liang's turmoil court regulations were abandoned and neglected; the judicial office followed precedent, kept them and did not reform; Yu was just about to change and expand them, making great regulations and broadly setting out the net, but the compilation was not finished, and therefore they are not listed in what follows.
translations.idiomatic: From Liang's final turmoil court regulations had collapsed; the judicial office clung to precedent without reform. Yu was about to overhaul them with broad new regulations, but the compilation was unfinished, and therefore they are not listed below.

sentences.zh: 及卒，太子親製誌銘，以表惟舊。

translations.literal: When he died the Heir Apparent personally composed his epitaph to show remembrance of old ties.
translations.idiomatic: When he died the heir apparent personally composed his epitaph in remembrance of old ties.

sentences.zh: 至德二年，追贈祕書監。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide he was posthumously enfeoffed as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide year 2 (584) he was posthumously made director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 所製章奏雜文二百餘篇，皆切事理，由是見重於時。

translations.literal: Memorials and miscellaneous writings he composed, more than two hundred pieces, all hit the facts of affairs, and on this account he was valued in his time.
translations.idiomatic: More than two hundred memorials and essays he wrote all addressed the facts of affairs, and on that account he was valued in his time.

sentences.zh: 子亮，有才學，官至尚書殿中侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Liang had talent and learning and reached Attendant in the Hall Directorate of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liang had talent and learning and rose to hall directorate attendant in the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 岑之敬

translations.literal: Qin Zhijing
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zhijing

sentences.zh: 岑之敬字思禮，南陽棘陽人也。

translations.literal: Qin Zhijing, styled Silin, was a native of Jiyang in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zhijing, styled Silin, came from Jiyang in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 父善紆，梁世以經學聞，官至吳寧令、司義郎。

translations.literal: His father Shanyu in the Liang era was known for classical learning and reached magistrate of Wuning and Director of the Office of Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shanyu was known in the Liang era for classical learning and rose to magistrate of Wuning and director of the office of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 之敬年五歲，讀孝經，每燒香正坐，親戚咸加歎異。

translations.literal: Zhijing at age five read the Classic of Filial Piety; each time he burned incense and sat upright, and kin all sighed in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijing at five read the Classic of Filial Piety; each time he burned incense and sat upright, and kin all marveled.

sentences.zh: 年十六，策春秋左氏制旨、孝經義，擢為高第。

translations.literal: At sixteen he was examined on the Exegesis of the Zuo Tradition to the Spring and Autumn Annals and the Meaning of the Classic of Filial Piety and was selected in the top grade.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he was examined on the Zuo Tradition exegesis and the meaning of the Classic of Filial Piety and placed in the top grade.

sentences.zh: 御史奏曰：「皇朝多士，例止明經，若顏、閔之流，乃應高第。

translations.literal: The Imperial Censor memorialized: "The imperial court has many scholars, but as a rule they stop at understanding the Classics; men like Yan and Min ought to rank in the top grade.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial censor memorialized, "The court has many scholars who as a rule only pass the classics examination; men like Yan and Min ought to rank at the top."

sentences.zh: 」梁武帝省其策曰：「何妨我復有顏、閔邪？

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang examined his answers and said: "What harm if I too have a Yan and Min?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang read his answers and said, "What harm if I too have a Yan and Min?"

sentences.zh: 」因召入面試，令之敬昇講座，敕中書舍人朱异執孝經，唱士章，武帝親自論難。

translations.literal: " He then summoned him for a face-to-face examination, had Zhijing ascend the lecture seat, ordered Master of Writing Attendant Zhu Yi to hold the Classic of Filial Piety and intone the chapter for scholars, and the Emperor himself debated him.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned him for a face-to-face test, had Zhijing ascend the lecture seat, ordered master of writing attendant Zhu Yi to hold the Classic of Filial Piety and intone the chapter for scholars, and debated him himself.

sentences.zh: 之敬剖釋縱橫，應對如響，左右莫不嗟服。

translations.literal: Zhijing analyzed and explained freely in all directions and answered like an echo; none left or right failed to sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijing analyzed freely in every direction and answered like an echo; none present failed to admire him.

sentences.zh: 乃除童子奉車郎，賞賜優厚。

translations.literal: He was then made Gentleman of the Palace Carriage for Youth and richly rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Gentleman of the Palace Carriage for Youth and richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 十八，預重雲殿法會，時武帝親行香，熟視之敬曰：「未幾見兮，突而弁兮！

translations.literal: At eighteen he attended the Dharma assembly at Chongyun Hall; at the time Emperor Wu personally performed the incense rite, gazed long at Zhijing, and said: "Not long since I saw you, and suddenly you wear the cap!
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he attended the dharma assembly at Chongyun Hall; Emperor Wu personally performed the incense rite, gazed long at Zhijing, and said, "It seems but yesterday I saw you, and suddenly you wear the cap!"

sentences.zh: 」即日除太學限內博士。

translations.literal: " That same day he was made Erudite within the Imperial University quota.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he was made erudite within the imperial university quota.

sentences.zh: 尋為壽光學士、司義郎，又除武陵王安西府刑獄參軍事。

translations.literal: Shortly he was made Shouguang academician and Director of Righteousness, then again removed to criminal-prison adviser in the Prince of Wuling's western headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he was made Shouguang academician and director of righteousness, then criminal-prison adviser in the prince of Wuling's western headquarters.

sentences.zh: 太清元年，表請試吏，除南沙令。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiqing he memorialized requesting trial office and was made magistrate of Nansha.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiqing year 1 he memorialized to enter trial office and was made magistrate of Nansha.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，之敬率領所部，赴援京師。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Zhijing led his command to rush to relieve the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion Zhijing led his troops to relieve the capital.

sentences.zh: 至郡境，聞臺城陷，乃與眾辭訣，歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Reaching the commandery border, hearing the terrace city had fallen, he with his forces took leave and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: At the commandery border he heard the terrace city had fallen; he bade his men farewell and returned home.

sentences.zh: 承聖二年，除晉安王宣惠府中記室參軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chengsheng he was made recording secretary in the Pacification-hui Prince of Jin'an's household.
translations.idiomatic: In Chengsheng year 2 he was recording secretary in the pacification-hui prince of Jin'an's household.

sentences.zh: 是時蕭勃據嶺表，敕之敬宣旨慰喻，會江陵陷，仍留廣州。

translations.literal: At that time Xiao Bo held Lingbiao; an edict ordered Zhijing to proclaim the intent and comfort him. When Jiangling fell he still remained at Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Bo then held Lingbiao; Zhijing was ordered to proclaim the edict and reassure him. When Jiangling fell he stayed at Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 太建初，還朝，授東宮義省學士，太子素聞其名，尤降賞接。

translations.literal: Early in Taijian he returned to court and was appointed eastern-palace righteousness-bureau scholar; the crown prince had long heard his name and especially lowered himself to honor and receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taijian he returned to court as an eastern-palace righteousness-bureau scholar; the crown prince had long known his name and treated him with special favor.

sentences.zh: 累遷鄱陽王中衛府記室、鎮北府中錄事參軍、南臺治書侍御史、征南府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He was in succession promoted recording secretary in the Prince of Poyang's central guard headquarters, recorder within limits in the pacify-north headquarters, Southern Terrace investigating secretary attendant drafting reports, and staff adviser in the campaign-south headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through recording secretary in the prince of Poyang's central guard, recorder within limits in the pacify-north headquarters, southern terrace investigating secretary, and staff adviser in the campaign-south headquarters.

sentences.zh: 之敬始以經業進，而博涉文史，雅有詞筆，不為醇儒。

translations.literal: Zhijing at first advanced through classical studies, yet broadly traversed literature and history, elegantly possessed literary brush, and was not an orthodox Confucian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijing had entered through classical studies but ranged widely in literature and history, wrote well, and was no orthodox Confucian.

sentences.zh: 性謙謹，未嘗以才學矜物，接引後進，恂恂如也。

translations.literal: By nature modest and cautious, he never used talent and learning to condescend to others; he received and guided juniors, ever earnest and agreeable.
translations.idiomatic: Modest and cautious by nature, he never flaunted his learning; he welcomed juniors and was always earnest and kindly.

sentences.zh: 每忌日營齋，必躬自洒掃，涕泣終日，士君子以篤行稱之。

translations.literal: On each anniversary of a parent's death he kept vegetarian observance, personally sprinkling and sweeping, weeping the whole day—gentlemen deemed him for earnest conduct.
translations.idiomatic: On each parent's anniversary he kept a vegetarian observance, swept the shrine himself, and wept all day; gentlemen praised his earnest conduct.

sentences.zh: 十一年卒，時年六十一。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he died, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 11, aged sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 太子嗟惜，賻贈甚厚。

translations.literal: The crown prince sighed in regret and sent funeral gifts very generously.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince mourned him and sent lavish funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷行於世。

translations.literal: He had a collection of ten juan circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: A collection of ten juan by him circulated.

sentences.zh: 子德潤，有父風，官至中軍吳興王記室。

translations.literal: His son Dekun had his father's manner and reached office as recording secretary to the Wu-xing Prince of the central army.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dekun had his father's manner and became recording secretary to the Wu-xing prince of the central army.

sentences.zh: 陸琰字溫玉，吏部尚書瓊之從父弟也。

translations.literal: Lu Yan, styled Wenyu, was a younger cousin of Minister of Personnel Qiong.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yan, styled Wenyu, was a younger cousin of Minister of Personnel Qiong.

sentences.zh: 父令公，梁中軍宣城王記室參軍。

translations.literal: His father Linggong was Liang recording secretary in the Prince of Xuancheng's central army headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His father Linggong was Liang recording secretary in the prince of Xuancheng's central army headquarters.

sentences.zh: 琰幼孤、好學，有志操。

translations.literal: Yan from childhood was orphaned, loved learning, and had resolve and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Yan loved learning and had firm resolve.

sentences.zh: 州舉秀才。

translations.literal: The province nominated him as outstanding candidate.
translations.idiomatic: The province nominated him as an outstanding candidate.

sentences.zh: 解褐宣惠始興王行參軍，累遷法曹外兵參軍，直嘉德殿學士。

translations.literal: On leaving the dark he was made acting secretary to the Pacification-hui Prince of Shixing, was in succession promoted to outer-army legal adviser, and straight academician of Jiadé Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On entering office he was acting secretary to the pacification-hui prince of Shixing, then outer-army legal adviser and a straight academician of Jiadé Hall.

sentences.zh: 世祖聽覽餘暇，頗留心史籍，以琰博學，善占誦，引置左右。

translations.literal: In his spare moments from audiences Emperor Wen paid considerable attention to historical records; because Yan was erudite and skilled at recitation, he was placed at his side.
translations.idiomatic: In spare moments from audiences Emperor Wen attended to historical records; finding Yan erudite and skilled at recitation, he kept him close.

sentences.zh: 嘗使製刀銘，琰援筆即成，無所點竄，世祖嗟賞久之，賜衣一襲。

translations.literal: Once he was ordered to compose an inscription for a knife; Yan took brush and finished at once without any emendation. Emperor Wen admired him long and granted one suit of robes.
translations.idiomatic: Once ordered to compose a knife inscription, Yan wrote it at a stroke without emendation. Emperor Wen admired him at length and granted a suit of robes.

sentences.zh: 俄兼通直散騎常侍，副琅邪王厚聘齊，及至鄴下而厚病卒，琰自為使主。

translations.literal: Shortly he was additionally made Regular Attendant through Direct Communication of the Scattered Cavalry, deputy to the Prince of Langya on a mission to hire Qi; when they reached Ye, Hou fell ill and died, and Yan himself became head of the mission.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he was also regular attendant through direct communication of the scattered cavalry, deputy to the prince of Langya on a mission to Qi; at Ye Hou fell ill and died, and Yan himself headed the mission.

sentences.zh: 時年二十餘，風神韶亮，占對閑敏，齊士大夫甚傾心焉。

translations.literal: He was then just over twenty; spirit and bearing were bright and clear, responses in audience relaxed and keen—the great officials of Qi very much inclined their hearts to him.
translations.idiomatic: He was then just over twenty, bright in spirit and bearing, quick and poised in reply; Qi officials greatly favored him.

sentences.zh: 還為雲麾新安王主簿，遷安成王長史，〔一八〕寧遠府記室參軍。

translations.literal: On return he was registrar of the Cloud-Banner Prince of Xin'an, promoted to chief steward of the Prince of Ancheng, [18] and recorder of the Ningyuan headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was registrar to the cloud-banner prince of Xin'an, then chief steward to the prince of Ancheng, [18] and recorder of the Ningyuan headquarters.

sentences.zh: 太建初，為武陵王明威府功曹史，兼東宮管記。

translations.literal: Early in Taijian he was merit-clerk of the Bright Prestige headquarters for the Prince of Wuling and concurrently eastern-palace recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taijian he was merit-clerk in the bright-prestige headquarters of the prince of Wuling and concurrently eastern-palace recorder.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂去官。

translations.literal: On his mother's mourning he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He left office on his mother's mourning.

sentences.zh: 五年卒，時年三十四。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died, aged thirty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 5, aged thirty-four.

sentences.zh: 太子甚傷悼之，手令舉哀，加其賻贈，又自製誌銘。

translations.literal: The crown prince deeply mourned him, personally ordered mourning rites, increased funeral gifts, and himself composed an epitaph inscription.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince mourned him deeply, ordered mourning by personal edict, increased funeral gifts, and wrote the epitaph himself.

sentences.zh: 至德二年，追贈司農卿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide he was posthumously made Director of the Court for Imperial Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide year 2 he was posthumously made director of the court for imperial granaries.

sentences.zh: 琰寡嗜慾，鮮矜競，遊心經籍，晏如也。

translations.literal: Yan had few desires and rarely competed for acclaim; his mind roamed classical texts, at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had few desires and rarely strove; his mind dwelt in the classics, at ease.

sentences.zh: 其所製文筆多不存本，後主求其遺文，撰成二卷。

translations.literal: Most of the writings he produced did not survive in the originals; Hou Zhu sought his surviving texts and compiled them into two juan.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his writings did not survive; Hou Zhu sought his remnants and compiled two juan.

sentences.zh: 有弟瑜。

translations.literal: He had a younger brother Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He had a younger brother Yu.

sentences.zh: 弟 瑜

translations.literal: Younger brother Yu
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Yu

sentences.zh: 瑜字幹玉。

translations.literal: Yu, styled Ganyu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, styled Ganyu.

sentences.zh: 少篤學，美詞藻。

translations.literal: From youth he was devoted to study and fine in literary craft.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he studied devotedly and wrote finely.

sentences.zh: 州舉秀才。

translations.literal: The province nominated him as outstanding candidate.
translations.idiomatic: The province nominated him as an outstanding candidate.

sentences.zh: 解褐驃騎安成王行參軍，轉軍師晉安王外兵參軍、東宮學士。

translations.literal: On leaving the dark he was made acting secretary to the Swift-cavalry Prince of Ancheng, transferred to army staff adviser for the Prince of Jin'an, and eastern-palace academician.
translations.idiomatic: On entering office he was acting secretary to the swift-cavalry prince of Ancheng, then staff adviser to the prince of Jin'an and an eastern-palace academician.

sentences.zh: 兄琰時為管記，並以才學娛侍左右，時人比之二應。

translations.literal: When his elder brother Yan was then recorder, both with talent and learning amused and attended left and right; people at the time compared them to the two Yings.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother Yan was recorder, both entertained the heir with their learning; contemporaries compared them to the two Yings.

sentences.zh: 太建二年，太子釋奠于太學，宮臣並賦詩，命瑜為序，文甚贍麗。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taijian the crown prince performed the offering at the imperial academy; palace officials all composed poems, and Yu was ordered to write the preface—the text very rich and elegant.
translations.idiomatic: In Taijian year 2 the crown prince offered at the imperial academy; palace officials all wrote poems, and Yu was ordered to compose the preface in rich, elegant prose.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書祠部郎中，丁母憂去職。

translations.literal: He was moved to bureau director of sacrifices in the Masters of Writing and on his mother's mourning left office.
translations.idiomatic: He was made bureau director of sacrifices in the masters of writing, then left office on his mother's mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋，為桂陽王明威將軍功曹史，兼東宮管記。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was merit-clerk of the Bright Prestige general headquarters for the Prince of Guiyang and concurrently eastern-palace recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was merit-clerk in the bright-prestige headquarters of the prince of Guiyang and concurrently eastern-palace recorder.

sentences.zh: 累遷永陽王文學、太子洗馬、中舍人。

translations.literal: He was in succession promoted literary scholar for the Prince of Yongyang, palace rhetorician, and attendant within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through literary scholar to the prince of Yongyang, palace rhetorician, and palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 瑜幼長讀書，晝夜不廢，聰敏彊記，一覽無復遺失。

translations.literal: Yu from childhood always read books day and night without ceasing, clever and with strong memory—one reading and nothing was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had read constantly from childhood, day and night; clever and with a strong memory, one reading left nothing lost.

sentences.zh: 嘗受莊、老於汝南周弘正，學成實論於僧滔法師，並通大旨。

translations.literal: He once received Zhuangzi and Laozi from Zhou Hongzheng of Runan and learned substantive discourse from the dharma master Monk Tao—both penetrated the great purport.
translations.idiomatic: He studied Zhuangzi and Laozi under Zhou Hongzheng of Runan and substantive discourse under the dharma master Monk Tao, mastering both.

sentences.zh: 時皇太子好學，欲博覽群書，以子集繁多，命瑜鈔撰，未就而卒，時年四十四。

translations.literal: At that time the heir apparent loved learning and wished to view all books broadly; because the zi and ji categories were numerous, he ordered Yu to excerpt and compile them—before it was finished Yu died, aged forty-four.
