translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent then loved learning and wished to survey all books; the zi and ji categories being vast, he ordered Yu to excerpt them, but Yu died before finishing, aged forty-four.

sentences.zh: 太子為之流涕，手令舉哀，官給喪事，并親製祭文，遣使者弔祭。

translations.literal: The crown prince wept for him, personally ordered mourning, the government supplied the funeral, and also personally composed sacrificial text and sent an envoy to offer condolence sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince wept for him, ordered mourning by personal edict, supplied the funeral from government funds, composed a sacrificial text, and sent an envoy to mourn.

sentences.zh: 〔一九〕仍與詹事江總書曰：「管記陸瑜，奄然殂化，悲傷悼惜，此情何已。

translations.literal: [19] He still wrote to Chamberlain Jiang Zong, saying: "Recorder Lu Yu has suddenly collapsed and transformed; grief, mourning, and cherishing—when will this feeling end?
translations.idiomatic: [19] He also wrote to chamberlain Jiang Zong: "Recorder Lu Yu has suddenly died; grief and mourning—when can it end?

sentences.zh: 吾生平愛好，卿等所悉，自以學涉儒雅，不逮古人，欽賢慕士，是情尤篤。

translations.literal: My lifelong loves—you all know them; I myself consider my learning in Ru elegance not to reach the ancients, yet cherishing the worthy and admiring scholars—that feeling is especially deep.
translations.idiomatic: You know my lifelong pursuits; I find my Ru learning falls short of the ancients, yet in cherishing the worthy and admiring scholars my feeling runs especially deep.

sentences.zh: 梁室亂離，天下糜沸，書史殘缺，禮樂崩淪，晚生後學，匪無牆面，卓爾出群，斯人而已。

translations.literal: The Liang house was in turmoil and separation, the realm seethed; books and histories were incomplete, rites and music collapsed; among later-born later-learners it is not that none face the wall—but to stand out from the crowd, only this man.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang house was torn apart and the realm boiled; books and histories were broken, rites and music ruined; later students are not without learning by rote, but to stand out from the crowd—only this man.

sentences.zh: 吾識覽雖局，未曾以言議假人，至於片善小才，特用嗟賞。

translations.literal: Though my knowledge and view are narrow, I have never lent my voice in discussion to others; yet toward a scrap of virtue or a small talent I especially sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: My knowledge is narrow and I have never lent my voice in debate, yet toward the smallest talent I always sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 況復洪識奇士，此故忘言之地。

translations.literal: How much more for vast knowledge and extraordinary talent—this is truly a place where words are forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: How much more for vast learning and rare talent—here words fail.

sentences.zh: 論其博綜子史，諳究儒墨，經耳無遺，觸目成誦，一褒一貶，一激一揚，語玄析理，披文摘句，未嘗不聞者心伏，聽者解頤，會意相得，自以為布衣之賞。

translations.literal: Discussing his comprehensive mastery of the zi and shi, thorough study of Ru and Mo, nothing that reached his ear was lost, nothing his eye met but he could recite it—one praise, one blame, one stirring, one lifting; discoursing on the mysterious and analyzing principle, splitting texts and plucking sentences—never did the hearer not submit in heart or the listener unknit the cheeks; when meanings met, he reckoned it the reward of a plain-clothed friendship.
translations.idiomatic: In mastering zi and shi, in Ru and Mo, nothing heard was lost and nothing seen went unrecited; praise and blame, stir and lift, discourse on mystery and analysis of principle, splitting texts and plucking lines—hearers submitted and listeners smiled; when minds met, it was the reward of friendship among plain cloth.

sentences.zh: 吾監撫之暇，事隙之辰，頗用譚笑娛情，琴樽閒作，雅篇豔什，迭互鋒起。

translations.literal: In the leisure of my oversight duties, in the gaps between affairs, I quite used witty talk to soothe feeling, zithers and wine cups at ease, elegant pieces and lush stanzas rising in interchange like crossed blades.
translations.idiomatic: In the leisure of oversight, in gaps between affairs, we used wit to soothe the mood, zithers and cups at ease, elegant verses and lush stanzas crossing like blades.

sentences.zh: 每清風朗月，美景良辰，對群山之參差，望巨波之滉瀁，或翫新花，時觀落葉，既聽春鳥，又聆秋鴈，未嘗不促膝舉觴，連情發藻，且代琢磨，間以嘲謔，俱怡耳目，並留情致。

translations.literal: Whenever wind was clear and moon bright, scenery fine and season apt, facing the mountains' uneven heights and gazing at the great waves' vast overflow—or playing with fresh flowers, or watching fallen leaves, now hearing spring birds, now listening to autumn geese—never did we not bend knees and raise cups, join feeling and send forth compositions, taking turns at polishing, interspersed with banter, all pleasing ear and eye and alike staying in sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: Under clear wind and bright moon, fine scenes and apt seasons, facing jagged mountains and vast waves, playing with fresh flowers or watching fallen leaves, hearing spring birds or autumn geese—we always bent knee and raised cup, joined feeling and sent forth lines, polishing in turn with banter between, pleasing ear and eye and holding feeling alike.

sentences.zh: 自謂百年為速，朝露可傷，豈謂玉折蘭摧，遽從短運，為悲為恨，當復何言。

translations.literal: I myself thought a hundred years swift and morning dew cause for sorrow—who expected jade broken and orchid snapped, suddenly to follow a short fate? For grief and for regret, what more can be said?
translations.idiomatic: I thought a hundred years swift and morning dew a cause for sorrow—who expected jade to break and orchid to snap, suddenly cut off? For grief and regret, what more can be said?

sentences.zh: 遺跡餘文，觸目增泫，絕絃投筆，恆有酸恨。

translations.literal: Traces and surviving writings—each sight increases tears; breaking the lute-string and casting aside the brush, I constantly have sour regret.
translations.idiomatic: Traces and surviving writings move me to tears at every sight; breaking the lute-string and casting aside the brush, I constantly feel sour regret.

sentences.zh: 〔二０〕以卿同志，聊復敘懷，涕之無從，言不寫意。

translations.literal: [20] As you share the same intent, I briefly set forth my feelings; tears have no outlet, words cannot write the meaning."
translations.idiomatic: [20] As you share this intent I briefly lay out my feelings; tears have no outlet and words cannot hold the meaning."

sentences.zh: 」其見重如此。

translations.literal: People of the time esteemed him thus.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time esteemed him thus.

sentences.zh: 至德二年，追贈光祿卿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide he was posthumously made Director of the Palace for Imperial Luminaries.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide year 2 he was posthumously made director of the palace for imperial luminaries.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collection of ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collection of ten juan.

sentences.zh: 瑜有從父兄玠，從父弟琛。

translations.literal: Yu had an elder cousin's son Jie and a younger cousin's son Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had an elder cousin's son Jie and a younger cousin's son Chen.

sentences.zh: 玠字潤玉，梁大匠卿晏〔子〕之子。

translations.literal: Jie, styled Runyu, was son of Liang Director of the Grand Master of Works Yanzi [21].
translations.idiomatic: Jie, styled Runyu, was son of Liang director of the grand master of works Yanzi [21].

sentences.zh: 〔二一〕弘雅有識度，好學，能屬文。

translations.literal: [21] Refined and magnanimous in discernment, fond of learning, able to compose prose.
translations.idiomatic: [21] Refined and discerning, fond of learning, able to write prose.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，對策高第。

translations.literal: Nominated as outstanding candidate, in policy essay he ranked high.
translations.idiomatic: Nominated as outstanding candidate, he ranked high in the policy essay.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書袁樞薦之於世祖，超授衡陽王文學，直天保殿學士。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Yuan Shu recommended him to Emperor Wen; he was specially appointed literary scholar to the Prince of Hengyang and straight academician of Tianbao Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Yuan Shu recommended him to Emperor Wen; he was specially made literary scholar to the prince of Hengyang and straight academician of Tianbao Hall.

sentences.zh: 太建初，遷長沙王友，領記室。

translations.literal: Early in Taijian he was moved to friend of the Prince of Changsha and concurrently recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taijian he became friend to the prince of Changsha and concurrently recorder.

sentences.zh: 後主在東宮，聞甚名，徵為管記。

translations.literal: When Hou Zhu was in the Eastern Palace he heard Jie's fame and summoned him as recorder.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Zhu was in the eastern palace he heard of Jie and summoned him as recorder.

sentences.zh: 仍除中舍人，管記如故，甚見親待。

translations.literal: He was then made attendant within the palace, recorder as before, and greatly favored and treated with intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made palace attendant, still recorder, and greatly favored.

sentences.zh: 尋以疾失明，將還鄉里，太子解衣贈玠，為之流涕。

translations.literal: Shortly, through illness he lost his sight; about to return to his home district, the crown prince removed his own garment to give Jie and wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon illness blinded him; as he was to return home the crown prince gave him his own garment and wept.

sentences.zh: 八年卒，時年三十七。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died, aged thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in year 8, aged thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 有令舉哀，并加賵贈。

translations.literal: There was an order to observe mourning and funeral gifts were also increased.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered mourning and increased funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 至德二年，追贈少府卿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide he was posthumously made Director of the Palace for the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide year 2 he was posthumously made director of the palace for the imperial treasury.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collection of ten juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collection of ten juan.

sentences.zh: 琛字潔玉，宣毅臨川王長史丘公之子。

translations.literal: Chen, styled Jieyu, was son of Chief Steward Qiu of the Pacification-steadfast Prince of Linchuan's household.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, styled Jieyu, was son of chief steward Qiu in the pacification-steadfast prince of Linchuan's household.

sentences.zh: 少警俊，事後母以孝聞。

translations.literal: From youth alert and talented, he served his stepmother and was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Alert and talented from youth, he was famed for serving his stepmother filially.

sentences.zh: 世祖為會稽太守，琛年十八，上善政頌，甚有詞采，由此知名，舉秀才。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was administrator of Kuaiji, Chen was eighteen; he submitted a eulogy on good government, very rich in literary color, and thereby became famous and was nominated as outstanding candidate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen was Kuaiji administrator, Chen at eighteen submitted a eulogy on good government of fine literary color, won fame, and was nominated as outstanding candidate.

sentences.zh: 起家為衡陽王主簿，兼東宮管記。

translations.literal: On first taking office he was registrar to the Prince of Hengyang and concurrently eastern-palace recorder.
translations.idiomatic: On first taking office he was registrar to the prince of Hengyang and concurrently eastern-palace recorder.

sentences.zh: 歷豫章王文學，領記室，司徒主簿，直宣明殿學士。

translations.literal: He served in succession as literary scholar to the Prince of Yuzhang, concurrently recorder, registrar of the Minister of State, and straight academician of Xuanming Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He served as literary scholar to the prince of Yuzhang with concurrent recorder, minister of state registrar, and straight academician of Xuanming Hall.

sentences.zh: 尋遷尚書三公侍郎，兼通直散騎常侍，聘齊，還為司徒左西掾。

translations.literal: Shortly he was moved to vice director of the Three Excellencies in the Masters of Writing, concurrently Regular Attendant through Direct Communication of the Scattered Cavalry, on a mission to hire Qi; on return he was left western aide of the Minister of State.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he was vice director of the three excellencies in the masters of writing and regular attendant through direct communication on a mission to Qi; on return he was left western aide of the minister of state.

sentences.zh: 又掌東宮管記，太子愛琛才辯，深禮遇之。

translations.literal: He again held charge of the eastern-palace recorder; the crown prince loved Chen's talent in debate and treated him with deep courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: He again held the eastern-palace recorder; the crown prince loved his eloquence and treated him with deep courtesy.

sentences.zh: 後主嗣位，遷給事黃門侍郎、中書舍人，參掌機密。

translations.literal: When Hou Zhu succeeded to the throne he was moved to Supervisor of Attendants of the Yellow Gate and Secretariat Drafter Within the Palace, participating in confidential matters.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Zhu succeeded he was made supervisor of attendants of the yellow gate and secretariat drafter within the palace, sharing confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 琛性頗疏，坐漏洩禁中語，詔賜死，時年四十二。

translations.literal: Chen's nature was rather careless; he sat convicted of leaking forbidden-palace speech and was by edict granted death, aged forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Careless by nature, he was convicted of leaking palace secrets and was ordered to die, aged forty-two.

sentences.zh: 何之元

translations.literal: He Zhiyuan
translations.idiomatic: He Zhiyuan

sentences.zh: 何之元，廬江灊人也。

translations.literal: He Zhiyuan was a native of Qian in Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He Zhiyuan came from Qian in Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 祖僧達，齊南臺治書侍御史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sengda was Qi investigating secretary attendant drafting reports of the Southern Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sengda was Qi investigating secretary of the southern terrace.

sentences.zh: 父法勝，以行業聞。

translations.literal: His father Fasheng was famed for moral conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fasheng was famed for moral conduct.

sentences.zh: 之元幼好學，有才思，居喪過禮，為梁司空袁昂所重。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan from youth loved learning and had literary thought; in mourning his observance exceeded the rites, and he was valued by Liang Minister of Works Yuan Ang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan loved learning from youth and had literary gifts; his mourning observance exceeded the rites, and Liang Minister of Works Yuan Ang valued him.

sentences.zh: 天監末，昂表薦之，因得召見。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianjian era Ang memorialized recommending him, and he thereby obtained an audience.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianjian Ang memorialized recommending him, and he was summoned to audience.

sentences.zh: 解褐梁太尉臨川王揚州議曹從事史，尋轉主簿。

translations.literal: On leaving the dark he was made aide in the discussion bureau of Liang Grand Marshal the Prince of Linchuan's Yangzhou separate office, and shortly transferred to chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: On entering office he was aide in the discussion bureau of Liang grand marshal the prince of Linchuan's Yangzhou separate office, then chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 及昂為丹陽尹，辟為丹陽五官掾，總戶曹事。

translations.literal: When Ang became administrator of Danyang he summoned Zhiyuan as aide of the five offices of Danyang, in overall charge of the household-registration bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Ang became Danyang administrator he summoned Zhiyuan as aide of the five Danyang offices, overseeing the household-registration bureau.

sentences.zh: 尋除信義令。

translations.literal: Shortly he was made magistrate of Xinyi.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly he was made magistrate of Xinyi.

sentences.zh: 之元宗人敬容者，勢位隆重，頻相顧訪，之元終不造焉。

translations.literal: Among Zhiyuan's clansmen was Jingrong, whose power and position were weighty; he repeatedly paid calls, but Zhiyuan in the end never went to him.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Jingrong held weighty power and rank and called on him often, but Zhiyuan never returned the visits.

sentences.zh: 或問其故，之元曰：「昔楚人得寵於觀起，有馬者皆亡。

translations.literal: Someone asked the reason; Zhiyuan said: "In olden days a man of Chu won favor through Guan Qi, and those who had horses all perished.
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, Zhiyuan said, "Long ago a Chu man won favor through Guan Qi, and everyone who had horses perished.

sentences.zh: 夫德薄任隆，必近覆敗，吾恐不獲其利而招其禍。

translations.literal: When virtue is thin and position weighty, ruin is near; I fear I would not gain the benefit but would invite the calamity."
translations.idiomatic: When virtue is thin and office heavy, downfall is near; I fear I would gain no benefit but invite disaster."

sentences.zh: 」識者以是稱之。

translations.literal: Men of insight for this praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The discerning praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 會安西武陵王為益州刺史，以之元為安西刑獄參軍。

translations.literal: When the Anxi Prince of Wuling became inspector of Yizhou, Zhiyuan was made criminal-prison adviser in the Anxi headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the anxi prince of Wuling became Yizhou inspector, Zhiyuan was criminal-prison adviser in the anxi headquarters.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，武陵王以太尉承制，授南梁州

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion the Prince of Wuling, as Grand Marshal exercising regency, appointed Southern Liang province
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion the prince of Wuling, as grand marshal exercising regency, appointed him to Southern Liang province

translations.literal: (long)
translations.idiomatic: (long)

sentences.zh: 〔刺〕史、〔二二〕北巴西太守。

translations.literal: [inspector] [22] and grand administrator of Northern Baxi.
translations.idiomatic: inspector [22] and grand administrator of Northern Baxi.

sentences.zh: 武陵王自成都舉兵東下，之元與蜀中民庶抗表請無行，王以為沮眾，囚之元于艦中。

translations.literal: The Prince of Wuling raised troops eastward from Chengdu; Zhiyuan together with the people of Shu submitted memorials asking that he not march. The prince thought this discouraged the army and imprisoned Zhiyuan on the ship.
translations.idiomatic: The prince of Wuling marched east from Chengdu. Zhiyuan and the people of Shu jointly memorialized that he should not go. The prince took this as discouraging the troops and imprisoned Zhiyuan aboard his vessel.

sentences.zh: 及武陵兵敗，之元從邵陵太守劉恭之郡。

translations.literal: When the Wuling army was defeated, Zhiyuan followed the Shaoling prefect Liu Gong to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wuling army was defeated, Zhiyuan followed Shaoling prefect Liu Gong to his commandery.

sentences.zh: 〔二三〕俄而江陵陷，劉恭卒，王琳召為記室參軍。

translations.literal: [23] Before long Jiangling fell; Liu Gong died; Wang Lin summoned him as recorder of the staff.
translations.idiomatic: [23] Soon Jiangling fell. Liu Gong died, and Wang Lin summoned him as recorder of the staff.

sentences.zh: 梁敬帝冊琳為司空，之元除司空府諮議參軍，領記室。

translations.literal: Liang's Emperor Jing enfeoffed Lin as Minister of Works; Zhiyuan was made deliberator in the works ministry and concurrently recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's Emperor Jing made Lin minister of works. Zhiyuan was made deliberator in the works ministry and concurrently recorder.

sentences.zh: 記事之史，其流不一，編年之作，〔二四〕無若春秋，則魯史之書，非帝皇之籍也。

translations.literal: Histories that record events have more than one tradition; annalistic works—[24] none match the Spring and Autumn—then the history of Lu is not the register of emperors and kings.
translations.idiomatic: Histories that record events have more than one tradition; of annalistic works—[24] none match the Spring and Autumn—and the history of Lu is not the register of emperors and kings.

sentences.zh: 案三皇之簡為三墳，五帝之策為五典，此典義所由生也。

translations.literal: Examining it: the documents of the Three August Ones are the Three Mounds; the policies of the Five Thearchs are the Five Canons—this is whence the meaning of canon arose.
translations.idiomatic: The documents of the Three August Ones are the Three Mounds; the policies of the Five Thearchs are the Five Canons—whence the meaning of canon arose.

sentences.zh: 至乃尚書述唐帝為堯典，虞帝為舜典，斯又經文明據。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Documents describes the Tang emperor as the Canon of Yao and the Yu emperor as the Canon of Shun—this again is the textual basis of the classics.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents describes the Tang emperor as the Canon of Yao and the Yu emperor as the Canon of Shun—again the textual basis of the classics.

sentences.zh: 是以典之為義久矣哉。

translations.literal: Thus the meaning of canon has been long indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the meaning of canon is ancient indeed.

sentences.zh: 若夫馬史、班漢，述帝稱紀，自茲厥後，因相祖習。

translations.literal: As for Sima Qian's history and Ban Gu's Han, they narrate emperors and call it annals; from then on successors have followed one another in habit.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian's history and Ban Gu's Han narrate emperors under the title annals; since then successors have followed one another in habit.

sentences.zh: 及陳壽所撰，名之曰志，總其三國，分路揚鑣。

translations.literal: When Chen Shou composed his work he named it Records; it surveys the Three Kingdoms and each goes its separate way.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shou named his work Records; it surveys the Three Kingdoms, each going its separate way.

sentences.zh: 唯何法盛晉書變帝紀為帝典，既云師古，在理為優。

translations.literal: Only He Fasheng's Jin History changed imperial annals into imperial canons; since it is said to follow antiquity, in principle it is superior.
translations.idiomatic: Only He Fasheng's Jin History changed imperial annals into imperial canons; said to follow antiquity, in principle it is superior.

sentences.zh: 故今之所作，稱為梁典。

translations.literal: Therefore what is composed now is called the Liang Canon.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore what is composed now is called the Liang Canon.

sentences.zh: 梁有天下，自中大同以前，區宇寧晏，太清以後，寇盜交侵，首尾而言，未為盡美，故開此一書，分為六意。

translations.literal: Liang held the realm: from before the Zhongdatong era the domain was tranquil; after the Taqing era bandits and raiders pressed in one upon another—speaking from first to last, it was not wholly perfect. Hence this book is opened and divided into six sections.
translations.idiomatic: Liang held the realm: before Zhongdatong the domain was tranquil; after Taqing bandits and raiders pressed in turn—taken from first to last, it was not wholly perfect. Hence this book is opened and divided into six sections.

sentences.zh: 以高祖創基，因乎齊末，尋宗討本，起自永元，今以前如干卷為追述。

translations.literal: Because Liang Gaozu laid the foundation, following upon the end of Qi, tracing clan and seeking root, beginning from the Yongyuan era—what precedes the present, a certain number of scrolls, is retrospective narrative.
translations.idiomatic: Because Liang Gaozu laid the foundation, following the end of Qi, tracing clan and root from the Yongyuan era—the preceding such-and-such scrolls are retrospective narrative.

sentences.zh: 高祖生自布衣，長於弊俗，知風教之臧否，識民黎之情偽。

translations.literal: Liang Gaozu was born a commoner and grew up amid corrupt custom; he knew whether customs were sound or unsound and understood the people's truth and falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Gaozu was born a commoner and grew up amid corrupt custom; he knew whether customs were sound or unsound and understood the people's truth and falsehood.

sentences.zh: 爰逮君臨，弘斯政術，四紀之內，寔云殷阜。

translations.literal: When he came to rule the realm he enlarged this policy; within four reign-periods it was truly prosperous and rich.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to rule he enlarged this policy; within four reign-periods the realm was truly prosperous.

sentences.zh: 今以如干卷為太平。

translations.literal: Now a certain number of scrolls are titled Great Peace.
translations.idiomatic: Now such-and-such scrolls are titled Great Peace.

sentences.zh: 世不常夷，時無恆治，非自我後，仍屬橫流，今以如干卷為敘亂。

translations.literal: The age is not always peaceful and the times not always well governed; not only after me did disorder still belong—now a certain number of scrolls are titled Narrative of Disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The age is not always peaceful and times not always well governed; not only after me did disorder still belong—now such-and-such scrolls are titled Narrative of Disorder.

sentences.zh: 洎高祖晏駕之年，太宗幽辱之歲，謳歌獄訟，向西陝不向東都。

translations.literal: Down to the year Liang Gaozu died in his carriage and the year Liang Taizong suffered disgrace, songs of praise and prison litigation turned west to Shanxi and not east to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Down to the year Liang Gaozu died and Liang Taizong suffered disgrace, songs of praise and prison suits turned west to Shanxi, not east to the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 不庭之民，流逸之士，征伐禮樂，歸世祖不歸太宗。

translations.literal: People who would not attend court and wandering scholars—in campaigns, rites, and music—turned to Emperor Wen and not to Liang Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Those who would not attend court and wandering scholars—in campaigns, rites, and music—turned to Emperor Wen, not Liang Taizong.

sentences.zh: 撥亂反正，厥庸斯在，治定功成，其勳有屬。

translations.literal: To dispel disorder and return to the correct, the merit lies here; when order was settled and the work completed, the achievement had its owner.
translations.idiomatic: To dispel disorder and return to the correct, the merit lies here; when order was settled and the work completed, the achievement had its owner.

sentences.zh: 今以如干卷為世祖。

translations.literal: Now a certain number of scrolls are titled Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Now such-and-such scrolls are titled Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 至於四海困窮，五德升替，則敬皇紹立，仍以禪陳，今以如干卷為敬帝。

translations.literal: As for when the four seas were exhausted and the Five Virtues rose and fell, then Emperor Jing succeeded and still abdicated to Chen—now a certain number of scrolls are titled Emperor Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When the four seas were exhausted and the Five Virtues rose and fell, Emperor Jing succeeded and still abdicated to Chen—now such-and-such scrolls are titled Emperor Jing.

sentences.zh: 驃騎王琳，崇立後嗣，雖不達天命，然是其忠節，今以如干卷為後嗣主。

translations.literal: General of Agile Cavalry Wang Lin set up the successor lord; though he did not accord with Heaven's mandate, yet it was his loyalty and integrity—now a certain number of scrolls are titled the Successor Lord.
translations.idiomatic: General of agile cavalry Wang Lin set up the successor lord; though he did not accord with Heaven's mandate, it was his loyalty and integrity—now such-and-such scrolls are titled the Successor Lord.

sentences.zh: 至在太宗，雖加美謚，而大寶之號，世所不遵，蓋以拘於賊景故也。

translations.literal: As for Liang Taizong, though a fine posthumous title was added, the title Great Treasure was not followed in the world—probably because he was constrained by the rebel Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: As for Liang Taizong, though a fine posthumous title was added, the title Great Treasure was not followed in the world—probably because he was constrained by the rebel Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 承聖紀歷，自接太清，神筆詔書，非宜輒改，詳之後論，蓋有理焉。

translations.literal: The Chengsheng chronology, from connecting with Taqing onward, and divine-brush edicts and documents ought not be rashly altered; examined in the discussion at the end, there is reason in this.
translations.idiomatic: The Chengsheng chronology, from connecting with Taqing onward, and divine-brush edicts and documents ought not be rashly altered; examined in the discussion at the end, there is reason in this.

sentences.zh: 夫事有始終，人有業行，本末之閒，頗宜詮敘。

translations.literal: Affairs have beginning and end; people have occupation and conduct—between root and branch it is quite fitting to set forth and narrate.
translations.idiomatic: Affairs have beginning and end; people have occupation and conduct—between root and branch it is quite fitting to narrate.

sentences.zh: 案臧榮緒稱史無裁斷，猶起居注耳，由此而言，寔資詳悉。

translations.literal: Examining it: Zang Rongxu said histories without editorial judgment are like daily records—by this reasoning, full detail is truly required.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Rongxu said histories without editorial judgment are like daily records—by this reasoning, full detail is truly required.

sentences.zh: 又編年而舉其歲次者，蓋取分明而易尋也。

translations.literal: Moreover, annalistic works that give the year sequence do so to take clarity and easy searching.
translations.idiomatic: Annalistic works that give the year sequence do so for clarity and easy searching.

sentences.zh: 若夫獫狁孔熾，鯁我中原，始自一君，終為二主，事有相涉，言成混漫。

translations.literal: As for when the Xianyun were fiercely rampant and choked our central plains—beginning with one ruler, ending with two lords—affairs overlap and words become confused.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xianyun were fiercely rampant and choked the central plains—beginning with one ruler, ending with two lords—affairs overlap and words become confused.

sentences.zh: 今以未分之前為北魏，既分之後高氏所輔為東魏，宇文所挾為西魏，所以相分別也。

translations.literal: Now what precedes the division is called Northern Wei; after the division what the Gao clan supported is Eastern Wei and what the Yuwen clan held is Western Wei—thus they are distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: What precedes the division is called Northern Wei; after the division what the Gao supported is Eastern Wei and what the Yuwen held is Western Wei—thus they are distinguished.

sentences.zh: 重以蓋彰殊體，繁省異文，其閒損益，頗有凡例。

translations.literal: Moreover, because covering and revealing differ in form and complexity and simplicity differ in text, the reductions and additions between them have general examples.
translations.idiomatic: Because covering and revealing differ in form and complexity and simplicity differ in text, the reductions and additions between them have general examples.

sentences.zh: 禎明三年，京城陷，乃移居常州之晉陵縣。

translations.literal: In Zhenming year 3 the capital fell; he then moved his residence to Jinling county in Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 the capital fell; he then moved his residence to Jinling county in Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇十三年，卒于家。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Sui Kaichuang he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaichuang year 13 of Sui he died at home.

sentences.zh: 徐伯陽

translations.literal: Xu Boyang
translations.idiomatic: Xu Boyang

sentences.zh: 徐伯陽字隱忍，東海人也。

translations.literal: Xu Boyang, styled Yinren, was a man of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Boyang, styled Yinren, was from Donghai.

sentences.zh: 祖度之，齊南徐州議曹從事史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Duzhi was a Liang deliberator-attendant in the Southern Xuzhou staff office.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Duzhi was a Liang deliberator-attendant in the Southern Xuzhou staff office.

sentences.zh: 父僧權，梁東宮通事舍人，領祕書，以善書知名。

translations.literal: His father Sengquan was a Liang eastern-palace communications attendant, concurrently in charge of the secretariat, and was famed for skill in calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sengquan was a Liang eastern-palace communications attendant, concurrently in charge of the secretariat, and was famed for calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 伯陽敏而好學，善色養，進止有節。

translations.literal: Boyang was keen and loved learning, skilled in pleasing his parents in countenance, and in advance and retreat had measure.
translations.idiomatic: Boyang was keen and loved learning, skilled in pleasing his parents by countenance, and measured in advance and retreat.

sentences.zh: 年十五，以文筆稱。

translations.literal: At age fifteen he was famed for literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he was famed for literary composition.

sentences.zh: 學春秋左氏。

translations.literal: He studied the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 家有史書，所讀者近三千餘卷。

translations.literal: His household had historical books; what he read came to more than three thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His household had historical books; what he read came to more than three thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 試策高第，尚書板補梁河東王國右常侍、東宮學士、臨川嗣王府墨曹參軍。

translations.literal: In the examination he placed at the top; the Masters of Writing by board appointed him right ordinary attendant in the Liang Prince of Hedong's kingdom, eastern-palace scholar, and ink-bureau aide in the Prince of Linchuan's successor household.
translations.idiomatic: In the examination he placed at the top; the masters of writing by board appointed him right ordinary attendant in the Liang prince of Hedong's kingdom, eastern-palace scholar, and ink-bureau aide in the prince of Linchuan's successor household.

sentences.zh: 大同中，出為候官令，甚得民和。

translations.literal: In the Datong era he went out as magistrate of Houguan and greatly won the people's harmony.
translations.idiomatic: In the Datong era he went out as magistrate of Houguan and greatly won the people's harmony.

sentences.zh: 侯景之亂，伯陽浮海南至廣州，依於蕭勃。

translations.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Boyang crossed the sea south to Guangzhou and relied on Xiao Bo.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion Boyang crossed the sea south to Guangzhou and relied on Xiao Bo.

sentences.zh: 勃平還朝，仍將家屬之吳郡。

translations.literal: When Bo was pacified he returned to court and still took his family to Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Bo was pacified he returned to court and still took his family to Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 天嘉二年，詔侍晉安王讀。

translations.literal: In Tianchen year 2 an edict ordered him to attend on the Prince of Jin'an in reading.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianchen year 2 an edict ordered him to attend on the prince of Jin'an in reading.

sentences.zh: 尋除司空侯安都府記室參軍事，安都素聞其名，見之，降席為禮。

translations.literal: Soon he was made recorder of the staff in the Minister of Works Hou Andu's headquarters; Andu had long heard his name and, on meeting him, stepped down from his seat in courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made recorder of the staff in minister of works Hou Andu's headquarters. Andu had long heard his name and, on meeting him, stepped down from his seat in courtesy.

sentences.zh: 甘露降樂遊苑，詔賜安都，令伯陽為謝表，世祖覽而奇之。

translations.literal: Sweet dew fell in the Leyou Park; an edict granted it to Andu and ordered Boyang to draft the letter of thanks; Emperor Wen read it and was struck with wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Sweet dew fell in the Leyou Park; an edict granted it to Andu and ordered Boyang to draft the letter of thanks. Emperor Wen read it and was struck with wonder.

sentences.zh: 太建初，中記室李爽、記室張正見、左民郎賀徹、學士阮卓、黃門郎蕭詮、三公郎王由禮、處士馬樞、記室祖孫登、比部賀循、長史劉刪等為文會之友，後有蔡凝、劉助、陳暄、孔範亦預焉，皆一時之士也。

translations.literal: Early in Taijian, Central Recorder Li Shuang, Recorder Zhang Zhengjian, Left People Gentleman He Che, Scholar Ruan Zhuo, Yellow Gate Gentleman Xiao Quan, Three Excellencies Gentleman Wang Youli, Recluse Ma Shu, Recorder Zu Sundeng, Comparison Bureau He Xun, Chief Clerk Liu Shan, and others were friends in a literary gathering; later Cai Ning, Liu Zhu, Chen Xuan, and Kong Fan also joined—men of the age all together.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taijian, central recorder Li Shuang, recorder Zhang Zhengjian, left people gentleman He Che, scholar Ruan Zhuo, yellow gate gentleman Xiao Quan, three excellencies gentleman Wang Youli, recluse Ma Shu, recorder Zu Sundeng, comparison bureau He Xun, chief clerk Liu Shan, and others were friends in a literary gathering; later Cai Ning, Liu Zhu, Chen Xuan, and Kong Fan also joined—all men of the age.

sentences.zh: 遊宴賦詩，勒成卷軸，伯陽為其集序，盛傳於世。

translations.literal: At roaming feasts they composed fu and poetry and bound them into scrolls; Boyang wrote the preface for the collection, which spread widely in the world.
translations.idiomatic: At roaming feasts they composed fu and poetry and bound them into scrolls; Boyang wrote the preface for the collection, which spread widely in the world.

sentences.zh: 及新安王為南徐州刺史，除鎮北新安王府中記室參軍，兼南徐州別駕，帶東海郡丞。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Xin'an was inspector of South Xuzhou, he was made central recorder in the Pacify-the-North Prince of Xin'an's household and concurrently separate-office aide of South Xuzhou, with concurrent acting administrator of Donghai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince of Xin'an was inspector of South Xuzhou, he was made central recorder in the pacify-the-north prince of Xin'an's household and concurrently separate-office aide of South Xuzhou, with concurrent acting administrator of Donghai commandery.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽王為江州刺史，伯陽嘗奉使造焉，王率府僚與伯陽登匡嶺，置宴，酒酣，命筆賦劇韻二十，伯陽與祖孫登前成，王賜以奴婢雜物。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Poyang was inspector of Jiangzhou, Boyang once went on mission to visit him; the prince led his staff and Boyang to ascend Kuang Ridge and set a banquet. When the wine was deep he ordered brush and fu on twenty difficult rhymes; Boyang and Zu Sundeng finished first; the prince granted slaves and miscellaneous goods.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince of Poyang was inspector of Jiangzhou, Boyang once went on mission to visit him. The prince led his staff and Boyang up Kuang Ridge and set a banquet. When the wine was deep he ordered brush and fu on twenty difficult rhymes; Boyang and Zu Sundeng finished first, and the prince granted slaves and goods.

sentences.zh: 及新安王還京，除臨海嗣王府限外諮議參軍。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Xin'an returned to the capital, he was made supernumerary deliberator in the Prince of Linhai's successor household.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince of Xin'an returned to the capital, he was made supernumerary deliberator in the prince of Linhai's successor household.

sentences.zh: 十一年春，皇太子幸太學，詔新安王於辟雍發論語題，仍命伯陽為辟雍頌，甚見佳賞。

translations.literal: In the spring of year 11 the heir apparent visited the imperial university; an edict ordered the Prince of Xin'an at the Piyong to set a Lunyu topic, and Boyang was further ordered to compose the Piyong eulogy—he received excellent reward.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year 11 the heir apparent visited the imperial university; an edict ordered the prince of Xin'an at the Piyong to set a Lunyu topic, and Boyang was further ordered to compose the Piyong eulogy—he received excellent reward.

sentences.zh: 〔二五〕除鎮右新安王府諮議參軍事。

translations.literal: [25] He was made deliberator of the staff in the Pacify-the-Right Prince of Xin'an's household.
translations.idiomatic: [25] He was made deliberator of the staff in the pacify-the-right prince of Xin'an's household.

sentences.zh: 十三年，聞姊喪，發疾而卒，時年六十六。

translations.literal: In year 13 he heard of his elder sister's death, took ill, and died—age sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he heard of his elder sister's death, took ill, and died at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 張正見

translations.literal: Zhang Zhengjian
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhengjian

sentences.zh: 張正見字見賾，清河東武城人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhengjian, styled Jianze, was a man of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhengjian, styled Jianze, was from Dongwucheng in Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 祖蓋之，魏散騎常侍、勃海長樂二郡太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gaizhi was a Wei regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and governor of Bohai and Changle commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gaizhi was a Wei regular attendant of the scattered cavalry and governor of Bohai and Changle commanderies.

sentences.zh: 父脩禮，魏散騎侍郎，歸梁，仍拜本職，遷懷方太守。

translations.literal: His father Xiuli was a Wei regular attendant of the scattered cavalry; he returned to Liang and still received his former post, then was transferred to governor of Huaifang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiuli was a Wei regular attendant of the scattered cavalry; he returned to Liang and still received his former post, then was transferred to governor of Huaifang.

sentences.zh: 正見幼好學，有清才。

translations.literal: Zhengjian from youth loved learning and had pure talent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengjian from youth loved learning and had pure talent.

sentences.zh: 梁簡文在東宮，正見年十三，獻頌，簡文深贊賞之。

translations.literal: When Liang's Emperor Jianwen was in the eastern palace, Zhengjian at thirteen presented a eulogy; Jianwen deeply praised it.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang's Emperor Jianwen was in the eastern palace, Zhengjian at thirteen presented a eulogy; Jianwen deeply praised it.

sentences.zh: 簡文雅尚學業，每自昇座說經，正見嘗預講筵，請決疑義，吐納和順，進退詳雅，四座咸屬目焉。

translations.literal: Jianwen by nature esteemed scholarship; whenever he himself ascended the seat to explain the classics, Zhengjian often attended the lecture hall, requested resolution of doubtful meanings, spoke and received in harmony, advanced and retreated with detailed elegance—all four sides fixed their eyes on him.
translations.idiomatic: Jianwen by nature esteemed scholarship; whenever he ascended the seat to explain the classics, Zhengjian often attended the lecture hall, requested resolution of doubtful points, spoke and received in harmony, and advanced and retreated with detailed elegance—all four sides fixed their eyes on him.

sentences.zh: 太清初，射策高第，除邵陵王國左常侍。

translations.literal: Early in Taqing he placed at the top in the target-shooting examination and was made left ordinary attendant in the Prince of Shaoling's Liang kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taqing he placed at the top in the target-shooting examination and was made left ordinary attendant in the prince of Shaoling's Liang kingdom.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝立，拜通直散騎侍郎，遷彭澤令。

translations.literal: When Liang's Emperor Yuan took the throne, he was made direct regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, then transferred to magistrate of Pengze.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang's Emperor Yuan took the throne, he was made direct regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, then transferred to magistrate of Pengze.

sentences.zh: 屬梁季喪亂，避地於匡俗山，時焦僧度擁眾自保，遣使請交，正見懼之，遜辭延納，然以禮法自持，僧度亦雅相敬憚。

translations.literal: As Liang's end brought turmoil, he took refuge on Kuangsu Mountain; at the time Jiao Sengdu held the masses and kept himself secure, sent envoys to request alliance—Zhengjian feared this, declined with humble words yet extended acceptance, but still held himself by ritual and law; Sengdu also by refinement mutually respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: As Liang's end brought turmoil, he took refuge on Kuangsu Mountain. Jiao Sengdu then held the masses and kept himself secure and sent envoys to request alliance. Zhengjian feared this, declined with humble words yet extended acceptance, but still held himself by ritual and law; Sengdu also by refinement respected and feared him.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，詔正見還都，除鎮東鄱陽王府墨曹行參軍，兼衡陽王府長史。

translations.literal: When the Founder received the abdication, an edict summoned Zhengjian back to the capital; he was made acting aide in the ink bureau of the Pacify-the-East Prince of Poyang's household and concurrently chief clerk in the Prince of Hengyang's household.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder received the abdication, an edict summoned Zhengjian back to the capital; he was made acting aide in the ink bureau of the pacify-the-east prince of Poyang's household and concurrently chief clerk in the prince of Hengyang's household.

sentences.zh: 歷宜都王限外記室、撰史著士，帶尋陽郡丞。

translations.literal: He served in succession as supernumerary recorder in the Prince of Yidu's household and compiler-historian gentleman, with concurrent acting administrator of Xunyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as supernumerary recorder in the prince of Yidu's household and compiler-historian gentleman, with concurrent acting administrator of Xunyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書度支郎、通直散騎侍郎，著士如故。

translations.literal: By cumulative promotion he became gentleman of the revenue bureau in the Masters of Writing and direct regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, compiler-historian as before.
translations.idiomatic: By cumulative promotion he became gentleman of the revenue bureau in the masters of writing and direct regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, compiler-historian as before.

sentences.zh: 太建中卒，時年四十九。

translations.literal: He died in the Taijian era—age forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Taijian era at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 有集十四卷，其五言詩尤善，大行於世。

translations.literal: He had a collection in fourteen scrolls; his five-character poetry was especially fine and circulated widely in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He had a collection in fourteen scrolls; his five-character poetry was especially fine and circulated widely in the world.

sentences.zh: 蔡凝字子居，濟陽考城人也。

translations.literal: Cai Ning, styled Ziju, was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Ning, styled Ziju, was from Kaocheng in Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 祖撙，梁吏部尚書、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zun was a Liang minister of the masters of writing and golden-glow grandee.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zun was a Liang minister of the masters of writing and golden-glow grandee.

sentences.zh: 父彥高，梁給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Yangao was a Liang attendant in the yellow gate.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yangao was a Liang attendant in the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 凝年位未高，而才地為時所重，常端坐西齋，自非素貴名流，罕所交接，趣時者多譏焉。

translations.literal: Ning's rank and position were not yet high, but talent and standing were weighty in the age; he regularly sat upright in the western studio—unless they were by nature noble and famous, he rarely received them; those who curried favor often ridiculed him.
translations.idiomatic: Ning's rank and position were not yet high, but talent and standing were weighty in the age; he regularly sat upright in the western studio—unless they were by nature noble and famous, he rarely received them; those who curried favor often ridiculed him.

sentences.zh: 高宗常謂凝曰：「我欲用義興主婿錢肅為黃門郎，卿意何如？

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong once said to Ning: "I wish to use the Prince of Yixing's son-in-law Qian Su as yellow gate gentleman—what is your opinion?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong once said to Ning, "I wish to use the prince of Yixing's son-in-law Qian Su as yellow gate gentleman—what is your opinion?

sentences.zh: 」凝正色對曰：「帝鄉舊戚，恩由聖旨，則無所復問。

translations.literal: " Ning answered with stern countenance: "Kinsmen of the imperial district—if favor comes by imperial intent, then there is nothing further to ask.
translations.idiomatic: " Ning answered with stern countenance, "Kinsmen of the imperial district—if favor comes by imperial intent, there is nothing further to ask.

sentences.zh: 若格以僉議，黃散之職，故須人門兼美，惟陛下裁之。

translations.literal: If measured by collective deliberation, for the posts of yellow gate and scattered cavalry one needs combined excellence in family and person—only Your Majesty may judge.
translations.idiomatic: If measured by collective deliberation, for the posts of yellow gate and scattered cavalry one needs combined excellence in family and person—only Your Majesty may judge.

sentences.zh: 」高宗默然而止。

translations.literal: " Emperor Gaozong fell silent and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Gaozong fell silent and stopped.

sentences.zh: 肅聞而有憾，令義興主日譖之於高宗，尋免官，遷交阯。

translations.literal: Su heard and bore resentment; he had the Prince of Yixing daily slander him to Emperor Gaozong; soon he was removed from office and transferred to Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Su heard and bore resentment; he had the prince of Yixing daily slander him to Emperor Gaozong; soon Ning was removed from office and transferred to Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 頃之，追還。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 後主嗣位，授晉安王諮議參軍，轉給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Houzhu succeeded, he was made deliberator in the Prince of Jin'an's household, then transferred to attendant in the yellow gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Houzhu succeeded, he was made deliberator in the prince of Jin'an's household, then transferred to attendant in the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 後主嘗置酒會，群臣歡甚，將移醼於弘範宮，眾人咸從，唯凝與袁憲不行。

translations.literal: Houzhu once set a drinking party; the ministers were very merry and were about to move the feast to Hongfan Palace; the crowd all followed—only Ning and Yuan Xian would not go.
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu once set a drinking party; the ministers were very merry and were about to move the feast to Hongfan Palace; the crowd all followed—only Ning and Yuan Xian would not go.

sentences.zh: 後主曰：「卿何為者？

translations.literal: Houzhu said: "What are you doing?
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu said, "What are you doing?

sentences.zh: 」凝對曰：「長樂尊嚴，非酒後所過，臣不敢奉詔。

translations.literal: " Ning answered: "Changle's dignity is not to be passed after wine—your servant dare not accept the edict.
translations.idiomatic: " Ning answered, "Changle's dignity is not to be passed after wine—your servant dare not accept the edict.

sentences.zh: 」眾人失色。

translations.literal: " The crowd turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: " The crowd turned pale.

sentences.zh: 後主曰：「卿醉矣。

translations.literal: Houzhu said: "You are drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu said, "You are drunk.

sentences.zh: 」即令引出。

translations.literal: " He at once ordered him led out.
translations.idiomatic: " He at once ordered him led out.

sentences.zh: 他日，後主謂吏部尚書蔡徵曰：「蔡凝負地矜才，無所用也。

translations.literal: Another day Houzhu said to Minister of Personnel Cai Zheng: "Cai Ning relies on his standing and prides himself on talent—there is no use for him.
translations.idiomatic: Another day Houzhu said to minister of personnel Cai Zheng, "Cai Ning relies on his standing and prides himself on talent—there is no use for him.

sentences.zh: 」尋遷信威晉熙王府長史，鬱鬱不得志，乃喟然歎曰：「天道有廢興，夫子云『樂天知命』，斯理庶幾可達。

translations.literal: " Soon he was transferred to chief clerk in the Trust-the-Might Prince of Jinxi's household; depressed and without achieving his aim, he sighed and said: "Heaven's Way has decline and rise; the Master said 'rejoice in Heaven and know fate'—this principle can nearly be reached.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon he was transferred to chief clerk in the trust-the-might prince of Jinxi's household. Depressed and without achieving his aim, he sighed and said, "Heaven's Way has decline and rise; the Master said 'rejoice in Heaven and know fate'—this principle can nearly be reached.

sentences.zh: 」因製小室賦以見志，甚有辭理。

translations.literal: " He therefore composed the Little Chamber Fu to show his intent—very fine in reasoning and pattern.
translations.idiomatic: " He therefore composed the Little Chamber Fu to show his intent—very fine in reasoning and pattern.

sentences.zh: 陳亡入隋，道病卒，時年四十七。

translations.literal: When Chen perished he entered Sui; on the road he took ill and died—age forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen perished he entered Sui; on the road he took ill and died at forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 子君知頗知名。

translations.literal: His son Junzhi was quite well known.
translations.idiomatic: His son Junzhi was quite well known.

sentences.zh: 阮卓，陳留尉氏人。

translations.literal: Ruan Zhuo was a man of Weishi in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Zhuo was from Weishi in Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 祖詮，梁散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Quan was a Liang regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Quan was a Liang regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 父問道，梁寧遠岳陽王府記室參軍。

translations.literal: His father Wendao was a Liang recorder of the staff in the Pacify-the-Far Prince of Yueyang's household.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wendao was a Liang recorder of the staff in the pacify-the-far prince of Yueyang's household.

sentences.zh: 卓幼而聰敏，篤志經籍，善談論，尤工五言詩。

translations.literal: Zhuo from youth was clever and keen, devoted in aim to the classics, skilled in discourse, and especially expert in five-character poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo from youth was clever and keen, devoted in aim to the classics, skilled in discourse, and especially expert in five-character poetry.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，其父隨岳陽王出鎮江州，遇疾而卒，卓時年十五，自都奔赴，水漿不入口者累日。

translations.literal: His nature was utmost filial; his father followed the Prince of Yueyang out to garrison Jiangzhou, met illness, and died—Zhuo was then fifteen and rushed from the capital to attend him, for many days taking neither water nor gruel.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was utmost filial; his father followed the prince of Yueyang out to garrison Jiangzhou, met illness, and died—Zhuo was then fifteen and rushed from the capital to attend him, for many days taking neither water nor gruel.

sentences.zh: 屬侯景之亂，道路阻絕，卓冒履險艱，載喪柩還都。

translations.literal: As Hou Jing's rebellion came, the roads were cut off; Zhuo braved danger and hardship and carried the coffin back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: As Hou Jing's rebellion came, the roads were cut off; Zhuo braved danger and hardship and carried the coffin back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 在路遇賊，卓形容毀瘁，號哭自陳，賊哀而不殺之，仍護送出境。

translations.literal: On the road he met bandits; Zhuo was haggard and wretched, wailing and pleading his case; the bandits pitied him and did not kill him, but still escorted him out of the territory.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he met bandits. Zhuo was wasted and wretched, wailing and pleading his case; the bandits pitied him and did not kill him, but escorted him out of the territory.

sentences.zh: 及渡彭蠡湖，中流忽遇疾風，船幾沒者數四，卓仰天悲號，俄而風息，人皆以為孝感之至焉。

translations.literal: When he crossed Pengli Lake, midstream he suddenly met a violent wind; the boat nearly sank four times; Zhuo lamented to Heaven, and shortly the wind ceased—people all took it as the utmost reach of filial feeling moving Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing Pengli Lake, he met a sudden gale midstream and the boat nearly sank four times. Zhuo cried out to Heaven; the wind soon ceased, and all took it as filial feeling moving Heaven to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 叔陵之誅也，後主謂朝臣曰：「阮卓素不同逆，宜加旌異。

translations.literal: When Shuling was executed, Houzhu said to the court ministers: "Ruan Zhuo from of old was not one with the rebels; he should receive special honor and distinction.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuling was executed, Houzhu told the court, "Ruan Zhuo was never of the rebels; he should be specially honored."

sentences.zh: 」至德元年，入為德教殿學士。

translations.literal: " In Zhide year 1 he entered service as academician of the Hall of Virtue and Instruction.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide year 1 he entered as academician of the Hall of Virtue and Instruction.

sentences.zh: 尋兼通直散騎常侍，副王話聘隋。

translations.literal: Soon he was also made direct-and-plain attendant of the scattered cavalry, deputy to Wang Hua on the mission to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also direct-and-plain attendant of the scattered cavalry, deputy to Wang Hua on the mission to Sui.

sentences.zh: 隋主夙聞卓名，乃遣河東薛道衡、琅邪顏之推等，與卓談醼賦詩，賜遺加禮。

translations.literal: The Sui Emperor had long heard Zhuo's name and therefore sent Xue Daoheng of Hedong, Yan Zhitui of Langye, and others to feast and compose poetry with Zhuo, with gifts and courtesy added.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui Emperor had long heard of Zhuo and sent Xue Daoheng of Hedong, Yan Zhitui of Langye, and others to feast and compose poetry with him, with added gifts and courtesy.

sentences.zh: 還除招遠將軍、南海王府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: On return he was made General Who Draws Distant and staff adviser to the Prince of Nanhai's household.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was made general who draws distant and staff adviser to the prince of Nanhai's household.

sentences.zh: 以目疾不之官，退居里舍，改構亭宇，脩山池卉木，招致賓友，以文酒自娛。

translations.literal: Eye disease kept him from taking office; he retired to his village dwelling, rebuilt pavilions, repaired hill ponds and ornamental plants, gathered guests, and took literature and wine for his pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Eye disease kept him from office; he retired home, rebuilt pavilions, laid out ponds and gardens, gathered guests, and amused himself with books and wine.

sentences.zh: 禎明三年入于隋，行至江州，追感其父所終，因遘疾而卒，時年五十九。

translations.literal: In Zhenming year 3 he entered Sui; reaching Jiangzhou, moved by the place where his father had ended, he fell ill and died, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 3 he entered Sui; at Jiangzhou, moved by where his father had died, he fell ill and died at fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 時有武威陰鏗，字子堅，梁左衛將軍子春之子。

translations.literal: At the time there was Yin Keng of Wuwei, styled Zijian, son of Liang's Left Guard General Zichun.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yin Keng of Wuwei, styled Zijian, was son of Liang's left guard general Zichun.

sentences.zh: 幼聰慧，五歲能誦詩賦，日千言。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever; at five he could recite poetry and rhapsodies, a thousand characters a day.
translations.idiomatic: Clever from youth, at five he could recite poetry and rhapsodies—a thousand characters a day.

sentences.zh: 及長，博涉史傳，尤善五言詩，為當時所重。

translations.literal: When grown he was broadly versed in histories and records, especially skilled in five-character poetry, and was highly regarded in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he was broadly versed in histories and especially skilled in five-character poetry, highly regarded in his day.

sentences.zh: 釋褐梁湘東王法曹參軍。

translations.literal: On first appointment he was law-bureau officer in the Prince of Xiangdong's Liang kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: On first appointment he was law-bureau officer in the prince of Xiangdong's Liang kingdom.

sentences.zh: 天寒，鏗嘗與賓友宴飲，見行觴者，因回酒炙以授之，眾坐皆笑，鏗曰：「吾儕終日酣飲，而執爵者不知其味，非人情也。

translations.literal: In cold weather Keng once feasted with guests and drinking companions; seeing the wine-server pass by, he turned back roast meat and gave it to him; the whole company laughed. Keng said: "We spend the whole day in deep drinking, yet the cup-bearer does not know the taste—not human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: One cold day Keng feasted with guests; seeing the wine-server pass, he sent back roast meat for him. The company laughed. Keng said, "We drink all day, yet the cup-bearer never tastes the wine—not human feeling."

sentences.zh: 」及侯景之亂，鏗嘗為賊所擒，或救之獲免，鏗問其故，乃前所行觴者。

translations.literal: " When Hou Jing's rebellion came, Keng was once seized by bandits; someone rescued him and he was spared. Keng asked the reason—it was the wine-server of before.
translations.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion Keng was once seized by bandits; someone rescued him. He asked why—it was the wine-server from before.

sentences.zh: 天嘉中，為始興王府中錄事參軍。

translations.literal: In Tianchen he was recorder in the Prince of Shixing's household.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianchen he was recorder in the prince of Shixing's household.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘗醼群臣賦詩，徐陵言之於世祖，即日召鏗預醼，使賦新成安樂宮，鏗援筆便就，世祖甚歎賞之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen once banqueted the ministers and ordered them to compose poetry; Xu Ling spoke of him to Emperor Wen, and that same day Keng was summoned to the banquet and ordered to compose on the newly completed Ancheng Palace of Peace and Joy; Keng took brush and finished at once—Emperor Wen greatly admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen once banqueted the ministers for poetry; Xu Ling spoke of Keng to him, and that day Keng was summoned and told to compose on the new Ancheng Palace of Peace and Joy. He wrote at once, and Emperor Wen greatly admired him.

sentences.zh: 累遷招遠將軍、晉陵太守、員外散騎常侍，頃之卒。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly advanced to General Who Draws Distant, administrator of Jinling, and supernumerary irregular attendant of the scattered cavalry; shortly he died.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to general who draws distant, Jinling administrator, and supernumerary irregular attendant of the scattered cavalry; soon he died.

sentences.zh: 有集三卷行於世。

translations.literal: He had a collection of three scrolls in circulation in the world.
translations.idiomatic: A collection of three scrolls circulated in his time.

translations.literal: Appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫文學者，蓋人倫之所基歟？

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Literature—is it not the foundation of human relations?
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Literature—is it not the foundation of human relations?

sentences.zh: 是以君子異乎眾庶。

translations.literal: Thus the gentleman differs from the common multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the gentleman differs from the common multitude.

sentences.zh: 昔仲尼之論四科，始乎德行，終於文學，斯則聖人亦所貴也。

translations.literal: Formerly, in Confucius's discussion of the four categories, he began with virtue and ended with literature—this too the sage valued.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Confucius ranked four categories, beginning with virtue and ending with literature—the sage valued that too.

sentences.zh: 至如杜之偉之徒，值於休運，各展才用，之偉尤著美焉。

translations.literal: As for men like Du Zhiwei, they met a fortunate age and each displayed his talents; Zhiwei was especially distinguished in beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Du Zhiwei met a fortunate age and each showed his talent; Zhiwei was especially distinguished.

sentences.zh: 「江德操字德藻」或本「江德藻字德藻」，疑。

translations.literal: "Jiang Dezao styled Dezao"—or in some texts "Jiang Dezao styled Dezao"—is doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Whether the name reads Jiang Dezao (cao) styled Dezao or Jiang Dezao (zao) styled Dezao is doubtful.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

translations.literal: [1] Central Great Unity
translations.idiomatic: On "[1] Central Great Unity"

translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (same).

sentences.zh: 〔通〕元年梁武帝幸同泰寺捨身敕勉撰定儀註 按徐勉卒於大同元年，中大同在大同之後。

translations.literal: [Tong] year 1 Liang Emperor Wu at Tongtai Temple renounced the body and ordered Xu Mian to draft and fix the ritual regulations
translations.idiomatic: On "[Tong] year 1 Liang Emperor Wu at Tongtai Temple renounced the body and ordered Xu Mian to draft and fix the ritual regulations"

sentences.zh: 查梁書武帝紀，梁武帝於中大通元年九月幸同泰寺捨身，明「中大同」為「中大通」之訛，今據改。

translations.literal: Note: checking the Annals of Emperor Wu in the Book of Liang, Liang Emperor Wu in the ninth month of Zhongdatong year 1 went to Tongtai Temple and renounced the body—clearly "Central Great Unity" is an error for "Central Grand Passage"; now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Liang, Annals of Emperor Wu, has Liang Wudi renounce the body at Tongtai in the ninth month of Zhongdatong year 1; Central Great Unity is an error for Central Grand Passage and is now emended.

sentences.zh: 〔二〕 以之偉掌記室 「偉」字原本缺，據各本補。

translations.literal: [2] "made Zhiwei manage the secretariat"—the character "wei" was originally missing in the base text; supplied according to all editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "[2] made Zhiwei manage the secretariat": wei was missing in the base text and is supplied per all editions.

translations.literal: [3] "still attended Lin
translations.idiomatic: On "[3] still attended Lin"

translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (cheng).

sentences.zh: 〔城〕公讀 據梁書南郡王大連傳改。

translations.literal: [cheng] duke's study"—changed according to the Biography of the Prince of Southern Commandery, Dalian, in the Book of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: On "[cheng] duke's study": emended per the biography of Prince of Southern Commandery Dalian in the Book of Liang.

sentences.zh: 按孫吳赤烏中，析陵陽、石城二縣地置臨城縣，梁屬南陵郡。

translations.literal: Note: in Sun Wu's Chiwu era, territory of Lingyang and Shicheng counties was split off to establish Lincheng county; under Liang it belonged to Nanling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Sun Wu's Chiwu era, parts of Lingyang and Shicheng were split off as Lincheng county; under Liang it belonged to Nanling commandery.

sentences.zh: 〔四〕 〔大同〕七年 據南史補。

translations.idiomatic: On "[4] [Datong] seventh year": supplied per the Southern History.

sentences.zh: 〔五〕 時樂府無孔子顏子登哥詞 「哥」各本作「歌」。

translations.literal: [5] "at the time the Music Bureau lacked lyrics for Confucius and Yanzi ascending"—"ge" in all editions is written "song."
translations.idiomatic: On "[5] at the time the Music Bureau lacked lyrics for Confucius and Yanzi ascending": ge in all editions is written song.

sentences.zh: 按哥古歌字。

translations.literal: Note: ge is the ancient form of the character for song.
translations.idiomatic: Ge is the ancient form of the character for song.

sentences.zh: 〔六〕 臣無容遽變市朝 「變」元龜四六四作「戀」。

translations.literal: [6] "your servant has no room hastily to change market and court"—"change" in Yuan Gui 464 reads "cherish."
translations.idiomatic: On "[6] your servant has no room hastily to change market and court": change in Yuan Gui 464 reads cherish.

sentences.zh: 〔藻〕字德藻 據北監本、殿本及南史改。

translations.literal: [zao] styled Dezao"—changed according to the Northern Supervisory, Hall, and Southern History editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "[zao] styled Dezao": emended per the Northern Supervisory, Hall, and Southern History editions.

sentences.zh: 按本書總目、子目均作「德藻」，本傳後文亦同，洪頤楫諸史考異及張森楷校勘記並以作「德操」為誤。

translations.literal: Note: this book's general table of contents and sectional tables all read "Dezao," and the later text of this biography is the same; Hong Yijun's Collation of Various Histories and Zhang Senkai's collation notes alike treat writing "Dezao" as the error.
translations.idiomatic: This book's tables and this biography later read Dezao; Hong Yijun and Zhang Senkai both treat writing Dezao (cao) as the error.

sentences.zh: 〔八〕 天嘉四年至與中書郎劉師知使齊 按南康愍王曇朗傳，江德藻與劉師知奉使至齊迎曇朗喪柩，以天嘉三年春還都，則德藻等使齊當在天嘉三年前，「四年」疑「二年」之誤。

translations.literal: [8] "from Tianchen year 4 to together with Secretariat attendant Liu Shizhi on a mission to Qi"—according to the Biography of the Prince of Nan'ang, the Deposed, Tanlang, Jiang Dezao and Liu Shizhi went on a mission to Qi to escort Tanlang's coffin and returned to the capital in the spring of Tianchen year 3; therefore Dezao's mission to Qi should have been before year 3—"year 4" is probably an error for "year 2."
translations.idiomatic: On "[8] from Tianchen year 4 with Secretariat attendant Liu Shizhi on a mission to Qi": per the biography of Prince Nan'ang Tanlang, Dezao and Shizhi escorted the coffin from Qi and returned in spring of Tianchen year 3; the mission must have been before year 3—year 4 is probably year 2.

sentences.zh: 〔九〕 庾持字允德 「允德」南史作「元德」。

translations.literal: [9] "Yu Chi styled Yunde"—"Yunde" in the Southern History reads "Yuande."
translations.idiomatic: On "[9] Yu Chi styled Yunde": Yunde in the Southern History reads Yuande.

sentences.zh: 〔一０〕父〔沙〕彌 據北監本、汲本、殿本補。

translations.literal: [10] "father [Sha]mi"—supplied according to the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.
translations.idiomatic: On "[10] father [Sha]mi": supplied per the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions.

sentences.zh: 按庾沙彌梁書有傳。

translations.literal: Note: Yu Shami has a biography in the Book of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shami has a biography in the Book of Liang.

sentences.zh: 〔一一〕天監初世祖與持有舊 張森楷校勘記云：「高祖以天監二年生，世祖安得於天監初與持有舊？

translations.literal: [11] "early in Tianjian the Founder and Chi had old ties"—Zhang Senkai's collation note says: "The Founder was born in Tianjian year 2—how could the Founder at the beginning of Tianjian already have old ties with Chi?
translations.idiomatic: On "[11] early in Tianjian the Founder and Chi had old ties": Zhang Senkai's note says the Founder was born in Tianjian year 2—how could he already have old ties with Chi at the start of Tianjian?

sentences.zh: 此必誤也。

translations.literal: This must certainly be an error."
translations.idiomatic: This must certainly be an error."

sentences.zh: 」今按：以傳文敘事之次第推之，「天監」疑為「太清」之誤。

translations.literal: On further examination: judging by the sequence of events in the biography, "Tianjian" is probably an error for "Taiqing."
translations.idiomatic: On further examination, judging by the sequence of events in the biography, Tianjian is probably an error for Taiqing.

sentences.zh: 〔一二〕坐杖殺縣民免封 南史無「封」字。

translations.literal: [12] "punished for beating a county man to death and lost enfeoffment"—the Southern History lacks the character "enfeoffment."
translations.idiomatic: On "[12] punished for beating a county man to death and lost enfeoffment": the Southern History lacks enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 按上文言「世祖怒之，因坐免」，當是免去其尚書左丞，至此始免其封爵，「封」字非衍文。

translations.literal: Note: above it says "Emperor Wen was angry with him and therefore punished him by dismissal"—that was removal from Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; only here is his enfeoffment finally taken away—the character "enfeoffment" is not a spurious addition.
translations.idiomatic: Above, Emperor Wen's anger led to dismissal from left vice director; only here is enfeoffment finally lost—enfeoffment is not redundant.

sentences.zh: 〔一三〕

translations.idiomatic: Note 13.

translations.literal: (transfer)
translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (transfer).

sentences.zh: 〔還〕為給事黃門侍郎 據南史改。

translations.literal: [return] made Gentlemen Attendant of the Yellow Gate—changed according to the Southern History.
translations.idiomatic: On "[return] made Gentlemen Attendant of the Yellow Gate": emended per the Southern History.

sentences.zh: 按此言持免臨安令後，還都為給事黃門侍郎也。

translations.literal: Note: this refers to after Chi was removed as magistrate of Lin'an and returned to the capital as Gentlemen Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: After Chi left the Lin'an magistracy he returned to the capital as Gentlemen Attendant of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 「遷」與「還」形近而訛。

translations.literal: "Transfer" and "return" are graphically similar and were corrupted.
translations.idiomatic: Transfer and return are graphically similar and were corrupted.

sentences.zh: 〔一四〕解褐梁安東王行參軍 張森楷校勘記云：「梁無安東王，安東是將軍號，疑此『東』字下有脫文。」

translations.literal: [14] "on first appointment, staff officer in the Prince of Andong's Liang kingdom"—Zhang Senkai's collation note says: "Liang had no Prince of Andong; Andong is a general's title—probably there is lacuna after the character 'east.'"
translations.idiomatic: On "[14] on first appointment, staff officer in the Prince of Andong's Liang kingdom": Zhang Senkai notes Liang had no prince of Andong; Andong is a general's title—probably text is missing after east.

sentences.zh: 〔一五〕所司收僧辯及其子頠〔屍〕 據北監本、殿本及南史補。

translations.literal: [15] "the authorities collected Sengbian and his son Yan's [corpse]"—"corpse" supplied according to the Northern Supervisory, Hall editions, and Southern History.
translations.idiomatic: On "[15] the authorities collected Sengbian and his son Yan's [corpse]": corpse supplied per the Northern Supervisory, Hall editions, and Southern History.

sentences.zh: 〔一六〕相率以家財營葬

translations.idiomatic: On "[16] together used family wealth to arrange the funeral"

translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (implements).

sentences.zh: 〔一七〕遇有猛獸 「獸」北監本、汲本、殿本作「虎」，下同。

translations.literal: [17] "encountered a fierce beast"—"beast" in the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions reads "tiger," the same below.
translations.idiomatic: On "[17] encountered a fierce beast": beast in the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions reads tiger, the same below.

sentences.zh: 按南史亦作「獸」，蓋避唐諱。

translations.literal: Note: the Southern History also reads "beast"—probably to avoid Tang taboo.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern History also reads beast—probably Tang taboo avoidance.

sentences.zh: 作「虎」乃後人回改。

translations.literal: The reading "tiger" is a later restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Tiger is a later restoration.

sentences.zh: 〔一八〕遷安成王長史 「史」原本訛「子」，各本不訛，今改正。

translations.literal: [18] "transferred to chief administrator of the Prince of Ancheng"—"administrator" in the base text was wrongly written "son"; other editions are not wrong; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: On "[18] transferred to chief administrator of the Prince of Ancheng": administrator in the base text was wrongly written son; other editions are correct; now emended.

sentences.zh: 〔一九〕并親製祭文遣使者弔祭 北監本、汲本、殿本「文」上無「 祭」字，「使」下無「者」字。

translations.literal: [19] "together personally drafted a sacrificial text and sent an envoy to perform mourning sacrifice"—the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions lack the character "sacrifice" before "text," and lack "envoy" after "sent."
translations.idiomatic: On "[19] together personally drafted a sacrificial text and sent an envoy to perform mourning sacrifice": the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions lack sacrifice before text and envoy after sent.

sentences.zh: 〔二０〕恆有酸恨 「恨」北監本、汲本、殿本作「梗」。

translations.literal: [20] "always had sour resentment"—"resentment" in the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions reads "lump in the throat."
translations.idiomatic: On "[20] always had sour resentment": resentment in the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions reads lump in the throat.

sentences.zh: 〔二一〕梁大匠卿晏〔子〕之子 據南史補。

translations.literal: [21] "Liang Grand Master of Works Yan [zi]'s son"—"zi" supplied according to the Southern History.
translations.idiomatic: On "[21] Liang Grand Master of Works Yan [zi]'s son": zi supplied per the Southern History.

sentences.zh: 按梁書陸雲公傳，雲公有兄名晏子，即此晏子也。

translations.literal: Note: in the Biography of Lu Yungong in the Book of Liang, Yungong had an elder brother named Yanzi—this is that Yanzi.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Liang biography of Lu Yungong names an elder brother Yanzi—this Yanzi.

sentences.zh: 〔二二〕武陵王以太尉承制授南梁州

translations.literal: [22] "the Prince of Wuling, as Grand Marshal assuming the regency, appointed him to South Liang province
translations.idiomatic: On "[22] the Prince of Wuling, as Grand Marshal assuming the regency, appointed him to South Liang province"

translations.idiomatic: Collation variant: (chief).

translations.literal: [inspector]"—changed according to the Southern History.
translations.idiomatic: On "[inspector]": emended per the Southern History.

sentences.zh: 按州無長史。

translations.literal: Note: a province has no "chief administrator."
translations.idiomatic: A province has no chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 〔二三〕之元從邵陵太守劉恭之郡 「劉恭」南史作「劉棻」。

translations.literal: [23] "Zhiyuan followed Shaoling prefect Liu Gong to the commandery"—"Liu Gong" in the Southern History reads "Liu Fei."
translations.idiomatic: On "[23] Zhiyuan followed Shaoling prefect Liu Gong to the commandery": Liu Gong in the Southern History reads Liu Fei.

sentences.zh: 通鑑梁敬帝紹泰元年「邵陵太守劉棻將兵援江陵」，亦作「劉棻」。

translations.literal: The Comprehensive Mirror for Liang Emperor Jing, Shaotai year 1, also has "Shaoling prefect Liu Fei leading troops to relieve Jiangling"—again "Liu Fei."
translations.idiomatic: The Comprehensive Mirror, Liang Emperor Jing Shaotai year 1, also has Shaoling prefect Liu Fei leading troops to relieve Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 下同。

translations.literal: The same below.
translations.idiomatic: The same below.

sentences.zh: 〔二四〕編年之作 「編」原本訛「繼」，各本不訛，今改正。

translations.literal: [24] "annalistic composition"—"annal" in the base text was wrongly written "continue"; other editions are not wrong; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: On "[24] annalistic composition": annal in the base text was wrongly written continue; other editions are correct; now emended.

sentences.zh: 〔二五〕甚見佳賞 「佳」北監本、汲本、殿本作「嘉」。

translations.literal: [25] "greatly received fine appreciation"—"fine" in the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions reads "commendation."
translations.idiomatic: On "[25] greatly received fine appreciation": fine in the Northern Supervisory, Ji, and Hall editions reads commendation.
